The series also existed in parallel in a version for the Wii, where it relied on motion controls.

Culturally, it is one of the most significant crossovers in the history of games. The pairing of Mario and Sonic kicked off a long and commercially very successful series that returned with every subsequent Olympic Games and became a fixture of family gaming.

On the Nintendo DS, it is an ideal title for short but fun competition, whether alone or with friends. It is not a deep sports simulation, but as a historic milestone and a brisk party game, it has its firm place.

**Why play it:** The historically first meeting of Mario and Sonic in the form of a brisk Olympic party game, a symbolic milestone as well as fun for the whole family on the road.

3ds__super-mario-3d-land.article:
If there was one title with which Nintendo wanted to convince the world that stereoscopic 3D on a handheld console is not just a marketing gimmick, it would be Super Mario 3D Land. The game came out in 2011, shortly after the launch of the 3DS, at a time when the console desperately needed a strong reason to buy it. And Mario delivered that reason in full glory.

The ingenious idea lies in connecting two worlds. Super Mario 3D Land combines the freedom of the spatial games from the Mario Galaxy line with the firm, tight structure of the classic 2D platformers. Instead of sprawling open levels, you get short, dense and precisely designed sections with a flag at the end. What's more, the stereoscopic depth here is not just an ornament: jumping over chasms and judging distances work tangibly better thanks to the 3D effect, which made this game perhaps the most convincing demonstration of the whole technology.

The iconic Tanooki Suit, the raccoon-like costume from Super Mario Bros. 3 that lets Mario glide through the air and attack with his tail, also made a return. The Nintendo EAD team, led by Koichi Hayashida and producer Takashi Tezuka, tuned the controls to perfection, so every jump lands exactly where it should. On top of that, the game is not stingy with rewards: after finishing the eight basic worlds, a set of more challenging special levels opens up that will test even seasoned players.

Culturally, it was a pivotal moment. Super Mario 3D Land became the first true system seller for the 3DS and helped kick-start console sales after its launch had stalled. The game sold in the tens of millions of copies and ranks among the most successful titles of the entire platform. Critics received it enthusiastically, praising its freshness, pace and the way it meaningfully uses 3D.

The game's legacy is still visible today. The design approach of Super Mario 3D Land later led to Super Mario 3D World on the Wii U, which expanded the same style with multiplayer co-op. For many fans, this entry remains the moment when linear and spatial Mario first merged into one perfectly harmonized whole.

**Why play it:** Because it is the best proof that 3D on the 3DS made sense, and at the same time one of the best-tuned platformers of its generation.

3ds__mario-kart-7.article:
Shells, banana peels and that one damned blue shell right before the finish line. Mario Kart 7 brought all of this adrenaline-fueled anarchy to the 3DS and added something the series had not seen for a long time: racing not only on the ground, but also in the air and underwater.

The heart of the game remains the proven formula of arcade karts with item collecting, but the seventh entry expanded it significantly. Gliders let you soar after springing off a ramp above the track, and the underwater propeller lets your vehicle plow the ocean floor. For the first time, you can also assemble your own kart from parts, choose the body, wheels and glider, and fine-tune the handling to your style. Added to that is a first-person view with tilting of the whole console, which fully utilizes the 3DS gyroscope.

The development was handled by Nintendo EAD in collaboration with the British studio Retro Studios, the creators of the Metroid Prime series, who helped fine-tune the tracks and the visual side. The game came out at the end of 2011 and, besides new circuits, offered carefully remade classic tracks from previous entries. Online multiplayer for up to eight players and communities allowed you to test your skills against people all over the world.

Commercially, it was a huge success. Mario Kart 7 became one of the absolute best-selling titles of the entire console with sales well over ten million copies, placing it at the very top of the 3DS charts. Critics praised the smoothness, balance and clever use of the new mechanics, though some pointed out that it was more of a polishing of a familiar formula than a revolution.

For many players, the seventh entry is still synonymous with pocket-sized Mario Kart to this day. It introduced elements such as gliders and underwater passages that became a standard even for the later, mega-successful Mario Kart 8. It is the type of game you pull out on a train ride or on the couch with friends, and suddenly it is midnight.

**Why play it:** Perfectly accessible, addictive and still fun racing in your pocket, which on top of that laid the foundations of the modern shape of the series.

3ds__legend-of-zelda-link-between-worlds.article:
What if Link could turn into a painting on the wall and literally walk along it? This crazy idea stands at the very heart of The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds, a game that took a revered classic from 1991 and built something surprisingly bold on top of it.

The 2013 title is a loose sequel to A Link to the Past and takes place in the same world of Hyrule seen from a bird's-eye view. The fundamental novelty is the ability to merge with a wall and move in a two-dimensional plane, opening up paths that would otherwise remain unreachable. On top of that, stereoscopic 3D makes sense here; thanks to it, the depth of walls and chasms is superbly legible.

The boldest change, however, is the structure itself. Instead of the game gradually doling out equipment in a fixed order, it offers a system of renting and later buying items from the mysterious merchant Ravio. Thus, right from the start you have access to most of the tools and you can tackle the dungeons in almost any order. With this, Nintendo elegantly broke the series' long-standing rule of linear progression and foreshadowed the freedom it would later fully develop in Breath of the Wild.

Behind the game stand Nintendo EAD and director Hiromasa Shikata. The developers consciously built on nostalgia, but took care to make it a full-fledged new game, not a mere remake. Hyrule flows briskly at sixty frames per second even with 3D turned on, which was a technical feat on the console.

Critics reacted enthusiastically. A Link Between Worlds collected a number of high scores and appeared in the rankings of the best games of the year as well as the best 3DS titles ever. Reviewers highlighted the clever dungeon design, the freedom of progression and the perfect pacing. For many, it is one of the best-designed entries in the entire series.

**Why play it:** It combines the warm nostalgia of classic Zelda with a boldly modern approach to freedom and gameplay. Brilliant from the first to the last dungeon.

3ds__legend-of-zelda-ocarina-of-time-3d.article:
For an entire generation of players, Ocarina of Time is the game where they first understood what an epic adventure means. Ocarina of Time 3D from 2011 took this legendary title from the Nintendo 64 and brought it to the 3DS in a way that honors the original while still feeling fresh.

It is not a mere port, but a thorough remaster. The graphics went through a complete overhaul: the models, textures and environments are significantly more detailed, and the whole world of Hyrule suddenly looks the way many remembered it more in their memories than in reality. Stereoscopic 3D lends the temples and duels a pleasant depth, and the touch screen finally solves one of the biggest pains of the original, namely the constant switching of items and the musical instrument in the menu.

The core of the game remained untouched, and that is a good thing. It is still the story of young Link, who travels through time to stop the villain Ganondorf, solves ingenious puzzles in sprawling dungeons and plays melodies on the ocarina that change time and weather. The combat system with targeting of enemies, which Ocarina of Time made famous in its day, still works absolutely superbly. For the daring, the game added a Master Quest with shuffled and made harder dungeons and a mode with tougher battles.

The original game from 1998 is to this day considered one of the most influential titles in the history of the medium and for many years topped the charts of the best-rated games ever. The remaster for the 3DS, on which the studio Grezzo participated under Nintendo's supervision, did not disappoint this reputation in the slightest and reaped excellent reviews.

For new players, it is an ideal gateway into one of the greatest adventures in gaming history, and for those who remember it, the perfect excuse to return to Hyrule. Few remasters manage to please both groups at once so elegantly.

**Why play it:** The definitive form of one of the most important games of all time, tuned so that it shines even for today's players.

3ds__super-smash-bros-for-nintendo-3ds.article:
Smash Bros. in your pocket? For a long time it sounded like an unattainable dream. Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS from 2014, however, turned it into reality and for the first time brought Nintendo's everyone-against-everyone brawl to a portable console.

The principle remains unmistakable. Instead of removing lives, here the characters accumulate damage percentages, and the higher the percentage, the farther they fly off after the next hit, until they fly out of the arena. A giant roster of iconic heroes from Nintendo worlds as well as guest series enters the fights, and the chaos is multiplied by items falling from the sky and colorful arenas. The 3DS version also brought the exclusive Smash Run mode, in which players first wander through a labyrinth, collect upgrades and only then face off in a final duel.

Behind the game stand the studios Sora and Bandai Namco under the leadership of Masahiro Sakurai, the father of the entire series. A big challenge was to fit an extensive game onto a small screen while at the same time maintaining a smooth sixty frames per second for the fights themselves, which was achieved. On top of that, the game allowed a connection with the version for the Wii U, which came out shortly after it, so fans could transfer configured characters and add-ons between both platforms.

Culturally, it was a big event. For the first time, players could take Smash anywhere with them, and online battles as well as local multiplayer made the console a beloved companion for the road. Commercially, the game ranked among the best-selling titles of the 3DS and sold in many millions of copies.

Reviews were mostly very favorable. Critics marveled that such a complex and rich game fit onto a handheld console at all, and praised the number of characters, modes and the overall fun factor. Minor reservations were perhaps only directed at the smaller screen in some crowded arenas.

**Why play it:** The complete madness of the Smash Bros. brand, which for the first time you slip into your pocket and pull out anywhere and anytime.

3ds__animal-crossing-new-leaf.article:
You become the mayor. No elections, no campaign, you simply step off the train by mistake and the residents of the little town declare you their head straight away. That is how Animal Crossing: New Leaf begins, a game that turned relaxation into art and captivated millions of players all over the world.

New Leaf from 2012 is a life simulator without victory and without end. You live in a little town inhabited by cute animal neighbors, catch fish and insects, collect fossils, furnish your house and pay off an eternal mortgage to the raccoon Tom Nook. The fundamental novelty compared to older entries is precisely the role of mayor: newly you can build public projects, benches, bridges, fountains or a cafe, and thus shape the whole town according to your vision. The game runs in real time tied to the console's clock, so in the morning the sun shines, at night it is dark, and holidays arrive on their actual day.

The magic lies in the complete absence of pressure. No one is chasing you, you cannot lose anything. New Leaf is a game about small joys, about waiting for a rare bug, about decorating a room or about visiting a friend's town over the internet. It is precisely this coziness that made it an ideal title for relaxation and also for people who do not actually consider themselves gamers.

Behind the game stand Nintendo EAD and a team that has led the series from its roots on the Nintendo 64. New Leaf tuned the long-standing formula and added depth in the form of customization, thanks to which it became the most successful entry in the series until the arrival of the later New Horizons. It sold in very high numbers and became one of the pillars of the 3DS library.

Critics received the game warmly and highlighted its endless depth, charm and the way it cleverly uses real time and social connection. For many 3DS owners, New Leaf became a game they returned to day after day, sometimes for whole years at a time.

**Why play it:** The best digital escape from the hustle, where the only goal is to live life your own way and enjoy small everyday joys.

3ds__fire-emblem-awakening.article:
This game was supposed to be the last. The Fire Emblem series stood on the brink of its end, and Nintendo made it clear to the developers that if the new entry did not sell enough copies, the brand would be over. Fire Emblem: Awakening from 2012 not only survived, but literally resurrected the whole series to new life.

It is a tactical strategy with RPG elements, in which you command an army of units on a square grid and, in turns, plan every movement and attack. Traditionally, a harsh rule of permanent death reigns here: a fallen unit is irretrievably gone, which turns every decision into a tense gamble. Awakening, however, also introduced an optional Casual mode, where fallen allies return, thereby opening the door to less hardened players as well. A key mechanic is the system of relationships between characters: units fighting side by side build a bond with one another, gain bonuses and can even fall in love, marry and bring offspring into the world, who then themselves enter the battle.

Behind the game stands the studio Intelligent Systems in collaboration with Nintendo. The developers put everything into it, because they did not know whether they would get another chance, and the result was a game full of content, memorable characters and a gripping story about the fight with the dragon Grima and the manipulation of time. Stereoscopic 3D lent the battle animations a splendid flair.

The result exceeded all expectations. Awakening sold in numbers that older entries could only dream of, and became a commercial as well as a critical hit. With this, it saved the entire brand and steered it toward the popularity it enjoys today, which was confirmed by later entries and the mobile Fire Emblem Heroes.

Critics highlighted the depth of the tactics, the elaborate characters and the emotional power of the story. Many reviewers labeled the game one of the peaks of the genre as well as one of the best titles of the 3DS. For newcomers, it became an ideal gateway into the world of Fire Emblem.

**Why play it:** Gripping tactics where every turn truly matters, and a game that by itself saved an entire legendary series.

3ds__fire-emblem-fates.article:
You were raised by one family, but you were born into another. And now you have to choose whose side you will fight on. It is with this agonizing dilemma that Fire Emblem Fates begins, an ambitious tactical strategy that split its story into several separate paths at once.

Fates from 2015 builds on the success of Awakening and pushes its ideas further. The foundation remains turn-based strategy on a grid, permanent death of units and the system of relationships thanks to which characters form bonds and start families. The greatest daring, however, is the structure itself: the game came out in two main versions, Birthright and Conquest, depending on whether the hero joins the peaceful kingdom of Hoshido or the belligerent Nohr. A third, downloadable path, Revelation, then offers the option of not siding with either party. Each version, moreover, brings differently tuned gameplay: Birthright is more accessible and more generous with resources, while Conquest emphasizes harsher tactical challenges with limited means.

Behind the game stands, once again, the studio Intelligent Systems. After the commercial resurrection of the series with Awakening, it was given the room to experiment and decided to tell the story from multiple perspectives. Visually as well as mechanically, it is an evolution of the proven formula, supplemented with new options for managing your own base and deeper customization of the army.

Fates did well commercially and confirmed that the popularity of Awakening was no accident. The sales of the individual versions together reached millions of copies, and the Fire Emblem brand thus definitively established itself among Nintendo's most significant names. The split into multiple versions became the subject of lively discussions among fans as well as the media.

Critics appreciated above all the polished tactical gameplay; the more challenging Conquest in particular reaped praise for its thoughtful map design. Reviewers at the same time pointed out that the story does not reach the quality of the gameplay and that the split into multiple paid versions is a bold but disputable step. Nonetheless, it is one of the most extensive and deepest strategic experiences on the 3DS.

**Why play it:** Top-tier turn-based tactics with a bold choice of sides, offering dozens of hours of thoughtful battles and three different perspectives on a single conflict.

3ds__pokemon-x-y.article:
When the generation of Pokémon X and Y came out in October 2013, it meant more for the brand than just another pair of versions on a green meadow. It was the first main entry in the series that took place fully in 3D, and the first that came out worldwide practically simultaneously. With this, Game Freak definitively tipped the legendary pocket monsters from pixel squares into a polygonal world, without losing any of the soul for which people have been catching, training and trading for over two decades.

The story takes you to the Kalos region, clearly inspired by France and with a silhouette resembling Paris in the form of the radiant Lumiose City. Mechanically, the sixth generation brought fundamental novelties. A completely new type, Fairy, debuted here, which rewrote the age-old balance of battles and finally gave a meaningful counterweight to dragons. An even bigger wave, however, came with Mega Evolutions: a temporary, battle transformation of select Pokémon, which gave old favorites like Charizard or Mewtwo a new look and strategic depth.

Game Freak at the same time significantly opened up training. The Super Training and Pokémon-Amie features allowed even less die-hard players to fine-tune stats and build a relationship with their buddies through petting and minigames on the touch screen. The Player Search System online environment running constantly in the lower screen made trades and battles with people from all over the world a matter of a few touches.

In terms of development, it was an enormous leap. The transition to 3D meant a complete remaking of the models, animations and the way the camera moves through the world. The game started on a trio of new starter Pokémon and right from the beginning also offered one from the classic first generation, which was a clear bridge between nostalgia and a new era.

Commercially, it was an absolute success. Pokémon X and Y became one of the fastest-selling titles on the 3DS and rank among the most successful entries in the series ever, with sales over sixteen million copies. For many players, they remain the moment when Pokémon became a truly modern game.

**Why play it:** It is an elegant entry gateway into modern Pokémon, where a 3D world, the Fairy type and Mega Evolutions meet for the first time. Ideal for nostalgics as well as newcomers.

3ds__pokemon-sun-moon.article:
Pokémon Sun and Moon from 2016 were created for the brand's twentieth anniversary, and Game Freak decided not to play it safe. Instead of repeating the tried-and-true pattern, one of the boldest rewrites of the formula that the series had ever experienced arrived. The tropical Alola region, inspired by Hawaii, is not just a backdrop, but an environment that changes the very structure of the game.

The most visible change was the abolition of the traditional gyms. Instead of collecting badges, you go through the so-called Island Challenge, a series of trials with individual tribal leaders, which culminate in battles with mighty Totem Pokémon. This structure gave the story a different rhythm and atmosphere, and the storytelling here is unusually personal and sharply characterized.

Mechanically, the series brought regional Alolan Forms, that is, new variants of classic Pokémon adapted to the local environment, which pleased veterans longing for a fresh look at old familiar faces. The battles were enriched by Z-Moves, one-time devastating attacks activated by an effectful gesture, which gave the battles a dramatic climax. Pokémon Refresh, in turn, allowed you to care for your buddies and heal their conditions outside of battle.

Game Freak also cleaned up long-standing bad habits. The annoying hidden moves for moving around the map were replaced by the Poké Ride system, where you summon a specific animal as a means of transport. The game is thus smoother and less bound by an inventory of abilities. Visually, Alola radiates sunshine, colors and the relaxed atmosphere of the islands.

Commercially, it was one of the most successful launches in the history of the brand, with sales exceeding sixteen million copies, and Sun and Moon rank among the best-selling titles on the 3DS ever. For many players, it is the entry that most boldly shook up the established formula and showed that even after twenty years, Pokémon can surprise.

**Why play it:** It offers the boldest rewrite of the Pokémon formula, a fresh tropical Alola and regional forms of favorites. A great choice for anyone who wants the series in its most imaginative form.

3ds__pokemon-omega-ruby-alpha-sapphire.article:
For players who grew up on the Game Boy Advance, 2014 was a homecoming. Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire are full-fledged remakes of the classic 2002 titles Ruby and Sapphire, taking us back to the tropical Hoenn region, this time in the full polygonal splendor of the sixth generation.

Game Freak wasn't interested in a mere fresh coat of paint. Hoenn came alive in 3D visuals following on from X and Y, complete with Mega Evolutions, the Fairy type, and a modern interface. The old battle models, animations, and map were completely reworked, so a region that longtime fans carried in their heads as a pixelated landscape suddenly breathes with depth and color.

The remake also added entirely new content. The Delta Episode story arc expands the original narrative with a dramatic chapter involving a legendary Pokémon and a cosmic threat, giving the return to Hoenn its own reason to exist. Collectors were delighted by the DexNav, a clever tool for tracking down rare Pokémon with special abilities, and fans of exploration got to fly across the region on the back of a legendary dragon via Soaring.

Mechanically, the game benefits from everything the sixth generation introduced, but adds specific novelties for Hoenn, including the so-called Primal forms of the legendary Kyogre and Groudon. This transformation elevates the clashes with these mythical beings to a new level of spectacle and power.

Commercially it was a huge success, and the remake ranks among the best-selling games on the 3DS, with sales topping fourteen million copies. For a generation that experienced Hoenn for the first time on a small glowing screen with no backlight, it's a gift full of both nostalgia and modern comfort.

**Why play it:** It's a nostalgic return to Hoenn in a modern coat with all the comforts of the sixth generation. For those who remember Ruby and Sapphire as well as for newcomers wanting the classic without compromise.

3ds__kid-icarus-uprising.article:
After more than two decades of silence, Pit, the winged angel in the service of the goddess Palutena, returned in 2012 in one of the most ambitious and, at the same time, most debated games on the 3DS. Kid Icarus: Uprising is a project by Masahiro Sakurai, creator of the Super Smash Bros. and Kirby series, and from the very first minute you can feel his obsession with action, humor, and dense design.

The game is split into two phases. The flight sections send Pit soaring through the air in the form of a flashy rail shooter packed with enemies, projectiles, and grandiose bosses. Once he touches down, it turns into a third-person action shooter where you move, dodge, and swap among dozens of different weapons, each behaving differently. The whole experience is accompanied by the constant, witty, and confidently chatty dialogue between Pit, Palutena, and other characters, which became legendary.

Its greatest pride is the Intensity system. Before each mission you bet in-game currency on the difficulty along a scale, and the higher you go, the tougher the fights and the richer the rewards awaiting you. This gambling mechanic gave the game enormous replayability and depth for those who want to conquer the peak of the challenge.

When it came to the controls, though, criticism clashed with admiration. Aiming with the stylus on the touchscreen while simultaneously moving with the slider was unfamiliar and even tiring for many, which is why Nintendo bundled a plastic stand with the game. Even so, the game won a strong fan base thanks to its energy, visual scope, and unexpected depth.

The package also included collectible AR cards which, once scanned by the 3DS camera, brought character battles to life in augmented reality, one of the most inventive demonstrations of the console's capabilities. Thanks to this game, Pit also returned to the wider public's awareness and became a fixture in the Super Smash Bros. series.

**Why play it:** It combines a brisk rail shooter, chatty action, and a gambling difficulty system into an unmistakable package. For players who want something quirky on the 3DS, brimming with personality.

3ds__luigi-s-mansion-dark-moon.article:
Luigi was never a brave hero, and that's exactly why it's so much fun to watch him tremble with fear in the dark halls of haunted mansions. Luigi's Mansion: Dark Moon from 2013 is the long-awaited sequel to the cult GameCube game, bringing Mario's adorably terrified brother back to the 3DS to battle ghosts once again.

Development was handled by Next Level Games, who took the original concept of hunting ghosts with the Poltergust vacuum and expanded it into a full-fledged adventure structure. Instead of one large mansion, you now explore several different locations, from a classic haunted house to snowy mountains or a mine, each with its own atmosphere, puzzles, and ghosts.

The core of the game is fighting phantoms. First you blind them with a flashlight, then you catch them in the vacuum's beam and, in a tense tug-of-war, suck them in. Added to this is solving ingenious puzzles, hunting for hidden treasures, and looking after Professor E. Gadd, who keeps giving Luigi tasks. The humor, lighting effects, and Luigi's frightened humming of melodies make the game's atmosphere something exceptional.

Dark Moon also brought a surprisingly robust multiplayer mode, ScareScraper, in which up to four players work together to fight their way up a tower full of ghosts. This cooperative mode significantly extended the game's lifespan and became a beloved part of the package.

Commercially it was a big success. The game sold many millions of copies and is among the best-selling titles on the 3DS, definitively confirming that Luigi can carry his own series. It was later followed by a third installment on the Switch, but this entry remains the one that restarted the brand and showed its potential.

**Why play it:** It offers an adorably spooky atmosphere, funny ghost hunting, and clever puzzles with a superb cooperative mode. Ideal for players who want Nintendo magic with a slight shiver down the spine.

3ds__star-fox-64-3d.article:
Some classics age like fine wine, and Star Fox 64 is one of them. Star Fox 64 3D from 2011 is a meticulous remake of the legendary Nintendo 64 rail shooter, bringing the flight squadron of the cosmic fox Fox McCloud to a handheld console in full polygonal splendor and with stereoscopic 3D that suits this genre like few others.

The foundation remained faithful to the original. You pilot the Arwing combat craft across dozens of missions throughout the galaxy, shooting down enemies, maneuvering between obstacles, and facing inventive bosses, while your teammates Falco, Peppy, and Slippy constantly report something over the radio. Famous lines like the celebrated „Do a barrel roll“ have gone down in gaming history and return here too.

Visually the game underwent a complete overhaul. The rough polygons of the original version were replaced by clean, detailed models, and the world feels far more alive. Stereoscopic 3D lends the battles a depth and sense of space that was missing before on a large screen. The nonlinear structure was also preserved, where the path through the galaxy branches according to your progress and performance, inviting repeated playthroughs.

The remake also added alternative motion-sensor controls, where you tilt the entire console, and a new multiplayer battle mode using the front cameras to show opponents' faces. An easier difficulty was prepared for newcomers, while veterans could play in a setting closer to the original.

Star Fox 64 3D served as a great example of how remakes of classics should look: respect for the source combined with sensitive modernization. For players who missed the original, it's the ideal entry point into one of Nintendo's most charismatic cosmic series.

**Why play it:** It's a perfectly modernized version of a classic rail shooter with stereoscopic 3D and the indestructible charm of the original. For nostalgics and newcomers alike craving brisk space action.

3ds__metroid-samus-returns.article:
Bounty hunter Samus Aran is one of the gaming world's icons, and yet she had to wait long years for a proper return in the classic 2D style. Metroid: Samus Returns from 2017 is a remake of the Game Boy game Metroid II, bringing the lonely hunt for alien metroids back to the 3DS in the form fans love.

Development was handled by the Spanish studio MercurySteam in collaboration with Nintendo, taking the ancient black-and-white title from 1991 and rebuilding it into a modern metroidvania. Your task is to descend deep into the interior of the planet SR388, explore its tangled tunnels, and gradually exterminate the metroids, which evolve here into ever more dangerous forms.

The most striking novelty is the counterattack system called the melee counter. When an enemy attacks you at the right moment, a well-timed strike stuns it and opens it up to a devastating shot. This mechanic gave the battles a rhythm and tension the original version lacked. There's also 360-degree aiming and the so-called Aeion abilities, such as scanning your surroundings or a temporary shield, which significantly deepened both exploration and combat.

Visually the game combines 2D gameplay with 3D models and backgrounds, giving the claustrophobic caves of planet SR388 a dense, gloomy atmosphere. Stereoscopic 3D emphasizes the depth of the environment and turns the lonely descent into darkness into an experience that holds the tension from start to finish.

For the series it was an important moment. After a long pause in the classic 2D line, it was proof that this form of Metroid still has a strong base, and it served as a harbinger of the highly acclaimed sequel Metroid Dread on the Switch. With this remake, MercurySteam earned the trust to keep developing one of the most influential gaming concepts of all.

**Why play it:** It brings back classic 2D Samus in a modern, polished metroidvania with a thrilling counterattack system. A great entry into the series and a reward for longtime fans.

3ds__monster-hunter-4-ultimate.article:
For many players in the West, this very title was the moment when they finally understood why the Monster Hunter series is such a phenomenon in Japan. Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate from Capcom arrived on the 3DS and brought with it a depth, addictiveness, and community spirit that can swallow up hundreds of hours.

The core of the game is wonderfully simple to grasp and infinitely complex to master. You hunt giant monsters, harvest materials from their bodies, and forge ever better weapons and armor from those materials so you can hunt even larger and more dangerous beasts. This looping cycle of preparation, hunting, and upgrading is the engine of the entire series, and here it runs at full throttle.

The fourth main installment brought a fundamental novelty in the form of verticality. For the first time you could climb walls, leap from heights, and land aerial attacks on monsters, giving battles an entirely new dimension. New weapon types were also added, such as the Insect Glaive for aerial acrobatics and the Charge Blade with its shifting combat style, expanding the already rich arsenal of fourteen distinct weapons, each of which plays like its own game.

The absolute heart of the experience, however, is cooperative hunting. Up to four players can team up and take down a monster together in tense, coordinated combat where timing, knowledge of the beast's behavior, and mutual support all matter. This game got countless communities on their feet and became an enormous social experience.

Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate became a commercial success outside Japan as well and played a key role in the series establishing itself on the global market. It laid the foundations for the later worldwide phenomenon Monster Hunter: World, and for many Western players it remains the game that pulled them into this addictive hunt.

**Why play it:** It offers the most addictive loop of hunting, forging, and upgrading with a superb co-op for up to four players. An ideal gateway into the world of Monster Hunter for anyone wanting depth measured in hundreds of hours.

3ds__monster-hunter-generations.article:
Imagine hunting a gigantic dragon, where every blow, every dodge, and every second spent sharpening your blade decides between life and death. Monster Hunter Generations is a celebration of everything that made the Monster Hunter series a phenomenon, and on the Nintendo 3DS it proves that depth of action doesn't require the power of next-generation consoles.

The core of the game is the loop fans know and love: you set out to hunt a giant beast, take it down after a long and exhausting battle, forge better armor and weapons from its materials, and head out after an even bigger opponent. Generations added to this formula the so-called Hunting Styles and Hunter Arts, that is, new sets of moves and special attacks that fundamentally change how each of the fourteen weapon classes handles. The game thus offers enormous freedom in how you build your hunter.

Monster Hunter Generations was developed and published by Capcom, which has held the series since its roots. The title was originally released in Japan under the name Monster Hunter X (Cross) and arrived in the West in 2016. It was a kind of celebratory compilation that gathered monsters and environments from previous installments and served them up in a new, significantly expanded form.

Culturally, the Monster Hunter series represents a genuine social phenomenon in Japan, where players gather for local cooperative hunts. Multiplayer is precisely the heart of the experience: with four people the hunt is far more manageable and at the same time socially gripping. Generations was later improved into the form of Monster Hunter Generations Ultimate for the Nintendo Switch, which added more demanding G-rank hunts and additional content.

Thanks to its combination of accessibility for newcomers and enormous depth for veterans, Generations ranks among the best-tuned installments on a handheld console. It's a game in which you can easily sink hundreds of hours without noticing.

**Why play it:** If you want to understand why the world fell for monster hunting, Generations is the ideal gateway, full of freedom, tactics, and unforgettable battles.

3ds__bravely-default.article:
Sometimes the best innovation hides in a return to the roots. Bravely Default took the classic structure of a Japanese RPG in the style of the early Final Fantasy games and breathed fresh life into it through a clever battle system and distinctive presentation, which made it one of the most beloved titles on the Nintendo 3DS.

The heart of the game is turn-based combat built on the pair of commands Brave and Default, after which the game is named. Using Default, a character banks its turn and defends, while thanks to Brave it can act several times in a round ahead of schedule, albeit at the cost of borrowing future actions. This mechanic adds a layer of tactical risk and reward to battles. It's complemented by an extensive job system, in which characters switch between dozens of professions and combine their abilities into countless builds.

Bravely Default was developed by Silicon Studio and published by Square Enix; Tomoya Asano contributed to the design and Revo composed the music. The game came out in Japan in 2012 and reached the West in 2013 and 2014 respectively. Visually it stands out with hand-painted, watercolor town backdrops that lend the world a fairy-tale fragility.

Culturally, Bravely Default showed that there was still strong demand for the traditional JRPG and revived a genre many considered to be fading. Critics and players alike received the title very warmly, and the game became a commercial success that convinced Square Enix of the brand's viability.

Its success led to the sequel Bravely Second: End Layer and later to the standalone installment Bravely Default II for the Nintendo Switch. The series thus built its own firm place in the modern JRPG.

**Why play it:** For anyone longing for an honest, beautiful-looking Japanese RPG with an inventive battle system, Bravely Default is one of the best choices on the 3DS.

3ds__shin-megami-tensei-iv.article:
Post-apocalyptic Tokyo, demons lurking around every corner, and moral choices that will haunt you long after you turn off the console. Shin Megami Tensei IV is a dark, uncompromising JRPG that never stops testing your endurance or your conscience.

The game mechanics rest on the famous Press Turn system, where hitting an enemy's weakness rewards the player with extra turns, while a mistaken attack is harshly punished. Just as crucial is negotiating with demons: instead of merely defeating your opponents, you can persuade them to join your team and then fuse them into stronger beings. The battles are demanding and require preparation, planning, and humility.

The Shin Megami Tensei series is developed by the Japanese studio Atlus, and the fourth main installment came out in 2013. The game is famous for its mature, often unsettling atmosphere, which isn't afraid of themes of faith, order, and chaos. The player passes through a crossroads of the Law and Chaos ideologies, and their decisions shape which of the branching endings they'll see.

Culturally, SMT IV cemented Atlus's reputation as a creator of hardcore RPGs for demanding audiences and served as a darker counterpart to the lighter spin-off series Persona. For many Western players it was one of the first opportunities to fully taste the series' main line.

The game received a follow-up title, Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse, which offered a new story perspective in the same world and fine-tuned a number of the game systems.

**Why play it:** If you're looking for a tough, intellectually demanding JRPG with a bleak atmosphere and a deep demon system, SMT IV is an essential experience.

3ds__etrian-odyssey-iv.article:
Take a pencil and a stylus and set out into the depths of a forest you'll map with your own hands. Etrian Odyssey IV: Legends of the Titan revives the spirit of classic dungeon crawlers and turns cartography itself into the core of the gaming experience.

The series' most characteristic mechanic is hand-drawn mapmaking. As you make your way through a labyrinth in first-person view, you draw the walls, doors, traps, and landmarks on the 3DS's bottom screen. This feeling of discovery and gradually uncovering the unknown is unmistakable. Added to this is classic turn-based combat, assembling a party from various professions, and the dreaded creatures called FOEs, powerful enemies best avoided at first. The fourth installment also added the ability to fly in an airship and explore the world above ground.

The series is developed by the studio Atlus, and Etrian Odyssey IV came out in 2012 in Japan, and in the West in 2013. It was the first main installment built directly for the 3DS, benefiting from the more powerful hardware and the spatial effect. The game is also considered one of the most accessible entries into an otherwise relentlessly demanding series, in part thanks to an optional easier difficulty mode.

Culturally, Etrian Odyssey carries the torch of a genre reaching back to titles like Wizardry, and keeps alive a tradition that would otherwise have died out long ago. For many players it's one of the few modern series that takes this classic style truly seriously.

The series' success led to further installments and remakes and later to the collector's compilation Etrian Odyssey Origins on newer platforms.

**Why play it:** For fans of dungeon crawlers who long for a hand-drawn adventure full of tactics and discovery, Etrian Odyssey IV is the ideal gateway.

3ds__professor-layton-vs-phoenix-wright-.article:
What happens when two of the video game world's smartest detectives meet in a single game? Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney is a bold crossover encounter of two iconic series that combines puzzles with tense courtroom trials in one medieval, almost fairy-tale story.

The gameplay elegantly alternates between two proven approaches. In the Layton-style sections you solve logic puzzles, riddles, and brain teasers, just as the professor's fans are used to. In the Ace Attorney parts, on the other hand, you become a defense attorney, cross-examine witnesses, look for contradictions in their testimonies, and present evidence. The game also introduces an entirely new kind of trial, where you can question several witnesses at once.

Two studios collaborated on the game, joining their brands: Level-5, the creators of the Professor Layton series, and Capcom, home of Phoenix Wright. The title came out in Japan in 2012 and reached the West in 2014. The story brings both heroes to the mysterious town of Labyrinthia, where a fear of witchcraft reigns, thus linking two otherwise very different gaming identities.

Culturally, it's a rare example of a successful crossover that doesn't feel like a mere marketing move but respects both fan communities. The meeting of Professor Layton and Phoenix Wright was a long-dreamed-of wish among players, and its realization confirmed just how strong a position both series held in the puzzle and adventure genre.

Visually, the game benefited from animated cinematic sequences that make it feel like an interactive fantasy film, and the music and atmosphere heighten the mysterious mood of the entire adventure.

**Why play it:** If you love both puzzles and courtroom drama, this crossover offers the best of both worlds in one charming package.

3ds__phoenix-wright-ace-attorney-dual-de.article:
Objection! The famous attorney Phoenix Wright returns to the courtroom and brings with him one of the darkest and most dramatic chapters of the entire series. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies is a visual novel that once again proves the search for truth can be just as thrilling as any action game.

The gameplay is split into two phases. In the investigation part you gather evidence, search crime scenes, and question suspects. In the trial phase you then cross-examine witnesses and look for contradictions in their testimonies in order to reveal the truth and clear innocent clients. Dual Destinies added new investigative abilities to the proven formula, among them the Mood Matrix of the young lawyer Athena Cykes, which allows you to analyze witnesses' emotions.

The Ace Attorney series was created by Shu Takumi and is developed by Capcom. Dual Destinies came out in 2013 and was the first full-fledged main installment of the series built with 3D character models instead of the previous 2D pixel graphics. In the West the game was released primarily through digital distribution, which was a bold step for the brand at the time.

Culturally, the Ace Attorney series is among the flagships of the visual novel and courtroom drama genre, and its charismatic characters have won a devoted audience all over the world. Dual Destinies pushed the storyline a step further and brought back to the game a tense, at times downright gloomy atmosphere.

The game is distinguished by dramaturgically elaborate cases that gradually intertwine into one larger story, and by the characteristic humor and absurdity that set the series apart from the competition.

**Why play it:** For lovers of stories, dialogue, and detective plots, Dual Destinies is a gripping courtroom thriller full of twists and unforgettable characters.

3ds__resident-evil-revelations.article:
Trapped on an abandoned cruise ship, surrounded by mutating horrors, with ammunition supplies dwindling dangerously. Resident Evil: Revelations proved that a handheld console could deliver a truly chilling survival horror that need not feel inferior to its console siblings.

The game consciously returns to the series' roots, placing greater emphasis on atmosphere, exploration, and resource management than on pure action. The cramped corridors of the Queen Zenobia recall the claustrophobic environments of the original entries. A new addition is the Genesis scanner, which you use to scan your surroundings, find hidden items, and extract healing bonuses from enemies. Alongside the story campaign, the game also offers a cooperative Raid mode, which emphasizes replaying levels and upgrading weapons.

Resident Evil: Revelations was developed and published by Capcom, originally released on the Nintendo 3DS in 2012. Its story takes place between the events of Resident Evil 4 and 5 and brings beloved heroes Jill Valentine and Chris Redfield back into action within the BSAA organization.

Culturally, Revelations confirmed that the 3DS could handle even technically demanding, mature titles, and the game became one of the console's graphical showcases. Thanks to its positive reception, Capcom decided to port the title to a range of other platforms, from consoles and PC to newer generations.

The success also led to the sequel Resident Evil: Revelations 2, turning this side line into a fully-fledged sub-series that, for many fans, represented a return to what made classic Resident Evil so terrifying.

**Why play:** If you crave classic survival horror with an oppressive atmosphere and clever resource management, Revelations is among the very best on the 3DS.

3ds__kingdom-hearts-3d-dream-drop-distan.article:
Disney magic, characters from Final Fantasy, and an intertwined, dreamlike story that makes your head spin. Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance brought one of the most ambitious chapters of the famous series to the Nintendo 3DS, advancing its Keyblade-bearer mythology into dramatic preparation for the grand finale.

The gameplay is built on a brisk action RPG combat loop, in which you control Sora and Riku in battles full of flashy combos, magic, and acrobatics. The key innovation is the Drop system, which automatically switches between the two heroes during play, forcing you to progress through both storylines simultaneously. Another prominent element is the Dream Eaters, creatures both adorable and combat-ready that you raise and take into action instead of the traditional Disney companions. The series also became famous for its acrobatic Flowmotion system, which lends combat and world traversal unprecedented dynamism.

The Kingdom Hearts series is created by Square Enix in collaboration with Disney and is led by director Tetsuya Nomura. Dream Drop Distance was released in 2012, and within the series' complicated storyline it serves as the so-called Mark of Mastery exam, a key turning point heading toward the culmination in Kingdom Hearts III.

Culturally, the Kingdom Hearts series represents one of the most successful crossovers in gaming history, uniting the Square gaming world with timeless Disney worlds. Players traverse environments inspired by films such as Pinocchio, The Hunchback of Notre Dame, and Tron: Legacy.

Thanks to its positive reception, the game was later reworked and included in the collector's compilation Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue, making it accessible to home-console players as well and turning it into an important piece of the entire saga's puzzle.

**Why play:** For fans of the series, Dream Drop Distance is an indispensable chapter of the story, while for newcomers it is a charming demonstration of just how fresh an action RPG on the 3DS can be.

3ds__dragon-quest-viii.article:
There are JRPGs that define the genre, and then there is **Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King** – a fairy tale about a cursed king transformed into a grotesque creature, a jester imprisoned in the body of a frog, and a young guardsman who sets out to undo the evil wrought by the malevolent mage Dhoulmagus. When the series first stepped into a fully three-dimensional world, it did so with such grace that it became one of the most beloved entries in the entire saga. The Nintendo 3DS version brings this classic story to a handheld console and adds a host of improvements.

The core of the gameplay remains purely traditional: turn-based battles, careful party building, exploration of a vast continent by horse-drawn carriage and on foot, and that unmistakable charm where every village hides its own story. The game became famous for its skill system, in which you allocate points according to your preferred weapons, and for the ability to combine characters' abilities into powerful combined attacks. The bestiary was, of course, designed by the legendary **Akira Toriyama**, creator of Dragon Ball, whose hand gives every monster that adorably unhinged character.

Development-wise, this is the work of studio **Level-5**, which at the time elevated the series to an entirely new visual level. The cel-shaded graphics, which literally brought Toriyama's drawings to life, made a stunning impression even on the PlayStation 2. The music was composed by the series' resident composer **Koichi Sugiyama**, whose orchestral themes are among the finest that Japanese games have offered.

The 3DS version brings enticements for fans: two entirely new playable characters, a reworked and less demanding enemy encounter system (which you now see on the map), and additional content after completing the main storyline. The stereoscopic 3D effect of the small screen lends the sprawling plains and dungeons a pleasant depth, albeit at the cost of a lower resolution compared to the original console version.

Culturally, Dragon Quest VIII is among the milestones that helped the series break through to Western markets, where Dragon Quest traditionally stood in the shadow of Final Fantasy. For many players in Europe and America, it was the very first entry that drew them into this world. The story of loyalty, sacrifice, and redemption remains one of the best-written in the genre.

**Why play:** A timeless turn-based JRPG with Toriyama's artistic magic and a heartwarming story, enriched on the handheld with new characters and extra content.

3ds__mario-and-luigi-dream-team.article:
What happens when you fall asleep and your dream becomes a battlefield? **Mario & Luigi: Dream Team** builds its entire existence on this playful question – here Luigi sleeps like a log and his dreams materialize into fantastic worlds through which Mario fights his way in a battle against the bat-like villain Antasma and the eternal pest Bowser. It is the most bizarre, most inventive, and perhaps most personal chapter of this beloved spin-off of the hopping brothers.

The Mario & Luigi series is famous for cleverly combining turn-based RPG battles with nimble action elements – in every attack and defense you must correctly time your button press, so combat never slides into mechanical routine. Dream Team adds a split between the waking world and the dream dimension. In dreams, Luigi multiplies into a swarm of copies, forms platforms and puzzles, and the game fully utilizes both 3DS screens – the upper one for the dream world, the lower one for the sleeping Luigi, whom you literally poke with the stylus.

Behind the game stands studio **AlphaDream**, the resident creators of the entire series, who always let their distinctive humor shine through. The script bursts with wit, parodies genre clichés, and turns the perpetually frightened Luigi into an unexpected star. It is Luigi who drives most of the ideas, which makes Dream Team something of a celebration of the eternally overlooked brother in green.

Visually, the game benefits from a clean, colorful aesthetic, and the dream sections offer monumental scale moments where the screen tilts and you control a giant version of Luigi. These "Giant Battles" using the console's tilt are among the most striking things the handheld had to offer.

Dream Team is proof that even a lighthearted spin-off series can be inventive and technically ambitious. For 3DS owners it was one of the titles that fully demonstrated the possibilities of the two screens and the 3D effect. It is a game that does not take itself deadly seriously, and yet you feel craftsmanly care in every detail.

**Why play:** A witty and inventive RPG that turns Luigi's dreams into a playground of ideas and perfectly utilizes the 3DS hardware.

3ds__paper-mario-sticker-star.article:
A world made of paper, a hero as thin as a postcard, and battles fought using... stickers. **Paper Mario: Sticker Star** is a bold experiment that took the beloved series and turned it upside down. Whether you love it or rail against it, one thing is certain – this paper Mario ignited a passionate debate among fans that has not died down to this day.

The basic idea is brilliantly simple: everything in this world is cut out of paper and your main tool becomes stickers. You collect them, paste them into an album, and in turn-based battles you peel them off to perform an attack – except each sticker is single-use, so you must manage them carefully. Added to this are the so-called "Thing" stickers, materialized objects from the real world (scissors, a fan, a flashlight) that solve puzzles and bosses in unexpected ways.

The game is the work of studio **Intelligent Systems**, the resident authors of the Paper Mario series. Sticker Star was created under the supervision of developers who consciously decided to move away from the more story-rich predecessors and focus on the puzzle and collecting side. The result is a title that abandons the complex party system and original characters in favor of a clean, minimalist structure oriented around Mario himself.

Visually, Sticker Star is enchanting – the 3DS's stereoscopic 3D effect gives the paper world literally layered depth and a diorama look, where the scenery bends and folds out like a child's cut-out craft. The paper aesthetic is refined to perfection, from crumpled edges to shadows.

Culturally, Sticker Star is a fascinating case of a game that divided the community: for some it is a refreshing and adorable trifle, for others a step back from the series' narrative depth. Either way, it influenced the direction of subsequent entries and became the subject of endless discussions about where Paper Mario should have gone.

**Why play:** A visually enchanting paper puzzle game with the original sticker mechanic, ideal for players seeking a lighter pace and inventive puzzles.

3ds__donkey-kong-country-returns-3d.article:
A hulking gorilla, bananas on the horizon, and a horde of mischievous Tikis who hypnotize the jungle's animals – **Donkey Kong Country Returns 3D** is the return of one of the most challenging and best-tuned platformers of its generation to a handheld console. If you like platformers that spare you nothing and make every completed level feel like a hard-won victory, you are in the right place.

The core of the game is precision. Donkey Kong and his buddy Diddy race through dozens of levels full of explosive mines, hurtling mine carts, silhouette passages, and hulking bosses. The game became famous for its uncompromising difficulty and brilliant level design, where every jump, every swing on a vine, and every bounce off an enemy demands precise timing. Collectors will get their fill thanks to the hidden K-O-N-G letters and puzzle pieces hidden in every level.

The original game was created by the American studio **Retro Studios**, famous for the reboot of the Metroid Prime series, which dusted off the Donkey Kong Country series after years and restored its luster. The 3DS conversion was handled by studio **Monster Games**. The handheld version adds stereoscopic 3D depth, which suits the jungle's multilayered scenery marvelously, and above all a brand-new "New Mode" – an easier mode with extra hearts and items, intended to make the game accessible even to less hardened players.

Visually, it is a celebration of movement in the background: levels take place across several depth planes, where giant octopuses, falling boulders, or silhouettes at sunset intrude into the main action. Musically, the game quotes and arranges iconic melodies from the original SNES entries, which reliably strikes a chord of nostalgia in veterans.

Culturally, Donkey Kong Country Returns confirmed that the classic 2D platformer still has its firm place even in the modern era, and the 3DS version made it possible to take this honest challenge on the road. It is a game that respects the player's patience and rewards perseverance.

**Why play:** A masterfully tuned and challenging platformer with superb level design, on the 3DS supplemented with 3D depth and a friendlier mode for newcomers.

3ds__yoshi-s-new-island.article:
An adorable green dinosaur, a crying baby on its back, and a world that looks as though someone painted it with crayons and watercolors – **Yoshi's New Island** claims the legacy of one of the most beloved platformers of all time. It is a direct sequel to the legendary Yoshi's Island, which once again takes on the difficult task of carrying little Mario to safety.

The gameplay builds on the series' proven pillars: Yoshi swallows enemies with his long tongue, turns them into eggs, and then hurls those at distant switches, enemies, and treasures. A key mechanic is protecting the baby – when Yoshi takes a hit, Baby Mario floats up in a bubble and you must catch him within a time limit before the henchmen snatch him away. Added to this is the flutter jump and the traditional gobbling of melons, thanks to which Yoshi spits seeds, fire, or ice.

Studio **Arzest**, founded by original creators from the studio behind the first entry, worked on the 3DS version. New Island adds giant eggs capable of smashing through entire stretches of scenery and several levels using the console's tilt via the motion sensor. The stereoscopic 3D effect gives the hand-painted world a pleasant spatiality.

The visual style is the game's greatest asset – the scenery resembles a child's drawing in pastel and chalk, with rough paper textures and adorable details. This artistic approach continues the series' characteristic aesthetic, where charm and playfulness always took precedence over technical perfection.

Culturally, New Island banks on the enormous popularity of the Yoshi brand and on nostalgia for the original SNES game, which many consider one of the best platformers of the era. Although it bears the heavy burden of expectation in the shadow of its famous predecessor, it offers a gentle, accessible, and visually lovely ride that will especially please players seeking a relaxed but still inventive platformer.

**Why play:** A gentle, visually enchanting platformer with a pastel art style and classic Yoshi egg mechanics, ideal for casual and nostalgic players alike.

3ds__rhythm-heaven-megamix.article:
Sing along with frogs, cut hair in rhythm, knock baseballs precisely on the beat – and the best is yet to come. **Rhythm Heaven Megamix** is an explosion of pure, undiluted joy, a compilation of the best minigames from the entire series plus a heap of new ones, stitched together into one insanely catchy package. If there is a game guaranteed to brighten your day, this is the one.

The principle is brilliantly simple and at the same time devilishly addictive: each minigame is built on a single thing – feeling the rhythm. You press buttons on the exact beat, and crucially, often with your gaze averted from the visual action, guided only by the music and your hearing. Megamix gathers dozens of these "rhythm games" from previous entries (from Game Boy Advance, Nintendo DS, and Wii) and supplements them with new ones, connected by a central storyline full of adorably wacky characters.

The series is a child of studio **Nintendo SPD** and behind it stands the musician **Tsunku**, a Japanese pop icon and producer whose sense for a catchy melody permeates every single note of the game. It is his musical instinct that makes Rhythm Heaven something exceptional – the tunes burrow into your head and won't let go.

Megamix adds a new progression system, a rewards shop, and a shorter, friendlier difficulty curve, so it serves as an ideal gateway for newcomers. The controls were simplified to buttons (compared to the touch controls of the DS entry), which many players consider more precise.

Culturally, the series has built a devoted cult of fans thanks to its distinctive, surreally adorable aesthetic and unmistakable humor. Megamix is the most comprehensive declaration of love to this brand – a kind of best-of with extra reach that can entertain for five minutes or absorb you for hours.

**Why play:** An immensely catchy and funny rhythm compilation with Tsunku's melodies, perfect for short bursts of pure gaming joy as well as passionate chasing of a perfect score.

3ds__cave-story-3d.article:
A story written and programmed by a single person in their spare time became one of the most influential independent titles in gaming history – and **Cave Story** is shining proof of it. This melancholic, action-packed adventure platformer about a nameless robot awakening in underground caves gained cult status long before the term "indie game" was in vogue.

The gameplay is a classic combination of nimble action and exploration in the metroidvania style. You fight your way through branching caves, collect and upgrade various weapons, and gradually uncover a touching story about a nation of rabbit-like creatures called the Mimiga and a malevolent doctor. The weapon mechanic is unique: each weapon gains experience, but drops a level when you take a hit – so every injury hurts twice as much. The game is famous for its multiple endings and hidden areas for the most persistent players.

The original was created by Japanese developer **Daisuke "Pixel" Amaya** entirely alone over the course of five years and released for free in 2004. This act of pure creative passion inspired a whole generation of independent creators. The **Cave Story 3D** version for the Nintendo 3DS was created by studio **Nicalis** in collaboration with the author, converting the originally two-dimensional game into fully 3D-rendered scenery with stereoscopic depth.

This reinterpretation preserves the original gameplay but rebuilds the environments into spatial dioramas – caves, cemeteries, and laboratories now recede across several layers, and the handheld's 3D effect lends them tangible volume. The game also includes the option to switch to an arranged or original soundtrack, whose catchy chiptune melodies are among the icons of the indie scene.

Culturally, Cave Story foreshadowed an entire wave of independent games and proved that a single passionate creator can make a work comparable to the output of major studios. Its influence on the genre and on the entire indie culture is undeniable, and the 3DS version offers one way to experience this classic on the go.

**Why play:** A cult indie classic with a touching story and precise metroidvania gameplay, reworked on the 3DS into spatial scenery with stereoscopic depth.

3ds__shovel-knight.article:
A knight armed not with a sword but with a shovel, who bounces on enemies like Scrooge McDuck on his cane and collects treasures in levels that look straight out of the eight-bit era – **Shovel Knight** is a perfect loving tribute to the golden age of Nintendo that became a modern classic in its own right. This game proved that retro aesthetics are not just a nostalgic crutch, but a fully-fledged artistic language.

The gameplay masterfully blends the best of legends like Mega Man, DuckTales, Castlevania, and Super Mario Bros. 3. The burial knight digs his way through levels, jumps down on enemies with a bounce attack of his shovel, and collects gems, for which he upgrades his equipment. The game is famous for its flawless controls, inventive level design, and an unforgettable gallery of bosses – the Order of No Quarter. Added to this is a semi-open world map in the style of Super Mario 3 and little towns full of quirky characters.

Behind the game stands the American studio **Yacht Club Games**, which funded the project through Kickstarter and raised many times more than it asked for. The developers took enormous care with authenticity: the game honors the technical limitations of the NES but cleverly circumvents them where it makes sense, and the result is pixel-art graphics that look like a memory of eight-bit games – more beautiful than they actually were. The music was composed by **Jake Kaufman** with contributions from the legendary **Manami Matsumae**, composer of the original Mega Man.

The Nintendo 3DS version adds a stereoscopic 3D effect and use of the lower screen for the map and inventory. Shovel Knight was released on a staggering number of platforms and gradually expanded with standalone campaigns for individual bosses, turning a single game into an entire sprawling saga.

Culturally, Shovel Knight became the benchmark for how to make a retro game right – with respect for its models, but with modern artistic and gameplay sensibility. It reaped enthusiastic reviews and numerous awards and is still considered one of the best indie titles ever.

**Why play:** A flawless tribute to the eight-bit era with precise controls, inventive level design, and unforgettable bosses, on the 3DS supplemented with a 3D effect and use of the lower screen.

3ds__super-street-fighter-iv-3d-edition.article:
When the Nintendo 3DS hit the market, Capcom was among the first to bet on its stereoscopic screen in grand style. **Super Street Fighter IV: 3D Edition** was part of the console's launch lineup and thus became the very first full-fledged Street Fighter in your pocket that was not merely a trimmed-down version, but a true port of the ambitious fourth-generation fighting game.

The core of the game remains faithful to its arcade and console predecessors. You will find a complete roster of over thirty fighters from Ryu and Chun-Li to characters added in the Super edition, an elaborate system of Focus Attacks, EX moves, super combos, and devastating Ultra Combos. Capcom became famous for building its combat system on readability and depth at the same time: even a beginner can manage a few blows, but mastery of timing, animation cancels, and reading the opponent runs deep.

Two essential innovations were added on the 3DS. The first is the so-called Dynamic View, a camera behind the fighter's back that uses the console's 3D effect and offers a striking close-up view of the fight. The second is the ability to map special moves to the touch screen, which makes the game accessible to players who do not want to wrestle with the precise input of quarter-circle motions on the small D-pad. For veterans, the classic side view and manual input remain.

The development context is key here. Street Fighter IV in 2008 practically resurrected the genre of 2D fighting games, which until then had been languishing, and returned it to mainstream attention. The 3D Edition carried this wave to the handheld and showed that even a demanding tournament fighter could work on the go. The game also supported local and online matches, so players could test their strength outside the campaign against the computer.

Culturally, Street Fighter remains one of the pillars of the entire esports and tournament fighting-game scene, whose events like EVO are watched by thousands of viewers. Having a full-blooded version of this saga right at the launch of a new Nintendo console was reason enough for many to buy it, and the game is still considered one of the more solid launch titles of the 3DS.

**Why play:** A full-fledged Street Fighter IV in your pocket with clever use of the 3D effect and touch controls that ease newcomers in without stripping away depth for veterans.

3ds__tekken-3d-prime-edition.article:
If Capcom staffed the 3DS with its Street Fighter, Namco could not stay behind with its flagship three-dimensional fighting game. **Tekken 3D: Prime Edition** brought the famous Iron Fist saga to the Nintendo handheld and used the stereoscopic screen to give the King of Iron Fist Tournament matches real spatial depth.

Tekken has always differed from its rivals in its conception of the combat system. Instead of universal buttons for weak and strong strikes, it works with controls per individual limb: each button corresponds to one hand or leg. From this grows an enormous repertoire of combinations, juggling the opponent in the air, and the characteristic moves of individual fighters. Prime Edition offers an extensive roster of characters drawing on the series' rich history, so fans will find their favorites across generations of the tournament.

The package had one more big draw, however. Alongside the game itself, it also contained the feature-length film **Tekken: Blood Vengeance** in a format that used the console's 3D screen. It was an ambitious attempt to combine interactive matches with an animated film and offer series fans a complete experience on a single cartridge. This combination of game and film was of an unusual kind on a handheld and made Prime Edition more of a collector's package than a mere port.

Development-wise, Tekken is among the longest-running and commercially most successful fighting games ever, and the Namco brand built an enormous fan base around it all over the world. Bringing such a technically demanding 3D fighter to a handheld console was no small task, and Prime Edition showed that the 3DS hardware was up to it.

Culturally, Tekken stands side by side with Street Fighter as one of the pillars of the fighting-game tournament scene. The 3DS version was not a full-fledged sequel to the main line, but for fans on the go it represented a welcome extension and proof that even on a small screen the Iron Fist could strike hard.

**Why play:** A spatial fighting game with its signature per-limb controls and a rich roster, plus the bundled animated film Blood Vengeance as a bonus for series fans.

3ds__mario-sports-superstars.article:
Nintendo has a long tradition of sending its mascots straight from adventures onto the sports field. **Mario Sports Superstars** takes this idea to the extreme: instead of a single discipline, it crams five different sports into a single title, making it a sort of festive mix for the whole family and for players on the go with the Nintendo 3DS.

The lineup is genuinely broad. Football, tennis, baseball, golf and horse racing, each discipline with its own rules, controls and pace. Mario's cast of characters, from Luigi through Peach and Yoshi to Bowser and Donkey Kong, appears across all the sports, so you can take your favorite hero onto the pitch as well as the green. The game aims for accessibility: the rules are easy to grasp, yet each discipline hides enough tactics to keep you entertained for the long haul.

A particularly interesting element is horse racing, where caring for your own horse, feeding and stroking it, feels closer to a light simulation than pure arcade. This discipline lends the otherwise brisk sports package a surprisingly calmer dimension. Football and baseball, by contrast, bank on team action, while tennis and golf stay faithful to the tried-and-tested Nintendo recipes that series like Mario Tennis and Mario Golf have honed over the years.

In terms of development, the game follows a long line of Mario sports titles that Nintendo has been releasing practically since the days of the Nintendo 64. Merging five distinct sports into a single title meant balancing the fun and depth of each one so that none felt like a hastily thrown-in side dish. The game also supported local and online matches for players who wanted to test their skills against others.

Culturally, Mario Sports Superstars fits neatly into the proven concept of Mario party games designed to appeal to a broad family audience. It isn't a title that breaks records for depth in any individual discipline, but as a five-pack of accessible sporting fun featuring the best-known mascots in the gaming world, it fulfills its purpose without a hitch.

**Why play:** Five sports in one with the whole Mario crew, ideal for family-friendly, accessible fun on the 3DS, where everyone can find their favorite discipline.

nes__super-mario-bros-3.teaser: One of the greatest platformers in history; the genre's benchmark of quality.
nes__super-mario-bros-3.detail: Under the leadership of Miyamoto and Tezuka, one of the finest platformers ever came to life, and the best-selling non-bundled NES game (over 17 million). It introduced a world map, costumes that change your abilities (tanuki, frog, boot) and enormous variety. In the US it was also made famous by the film The Wizard, which worked like one big advertising trailer. The design benchmark of the genre.
nes__super-mario-bros-3.article:
There exists a platformer that even people who had never heard of video games wanted to play, and its name is **Super Mario Bros. 3**. In America it was also made famous by the feature film The Wizard, which functioned like one big two-hour advertising trailer and stirred up mass hysteria even before the game reached stores. And when it did arrive, it showed just how far the genre could go.

Under the leadership of Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka, one of the greatest platformers ever came to life, and at the same time the best-selling non-bundled game for the NES, selling over **17 million copies**. That is no accident. The third installment introduced a world map that gave the adventure structure and a choice of routes, and above all costumes that change Mario's abilities: the tanuki, the frog, the boot and the legendary tanuki statue.

What is truly ingenious is the variety. Each of the worlds has its own theme, its own enemies and its own ideas that rarely repeat. The game constantly surprises you, and the moment you think you've seen everything, it throws a flying airship, a giant version of a familiar setting, or an entirely new trick at you. It is a nonstop stream of creativity of a kind you simply didn't see back then.

In terms of design, the third game set a bar that others had to clear for decades afterward. Precise controls, clean pacing and balanced difficulty turned it into the quality benchmark of the entire genre. Even today it holds true that if you want to explain what makes a platformer great, you simply point to Super Mario Bros. 3.

It is no wonder, then, that it appears at the top of practically every list of the best games in history and that its influence is felt to this day. It is the crowning work of the NES era and proof that Nintendo knew how to spark timeless fun from a simple concept.

**Why play:** Because it is one of the greatest platformers of all time, unsurpassed in variety, pacing and pure joy of play.

nes__super-mario-bros.teaser: The game that saved the games industry after the '83 crash.
nes__super-mario-bros.detail: The NES pack-in title that in the US practically resurrected the games market after the 1983 crash. Over 40 million copies were sold. Its first level (World 1-1) is a textbook example of 'level design as tutorial' — it teaches you all the mechanics without a single word of text. Miyamoto's revolution in movement and pacing.
nes__super-mario-bros.article:
One game, one plumber and one jump that changed the history of entertainment. **Super Mario Bros.** arrived in 1985 as a pack-in title for the NES and in the US practically resurrected a games market that had hit rock bottom after the 1983 crash. If there is a single game we can thank for the fact that we still have consoles at all, it is this one.

The numbers speak clearly: over **40 million copies** were sold, making it one of the best-selling games ever. But the real magic lies not in the numbers, but in the design. The famous first level, World 1-1, is still cited today as a textbook example of „level design as tutorial“ — it teaches you all the game's mechanics without a single word of text. A Goomba approaching from the right teaches you to jump, a question-mark block rewards you with a mushroom, a pipe tempts you to explore.

Miyamoto's revolution lay in movement and pacing. Mario has weight, inertia and precision, and running, jumping and braking respond so satisfyingly that the mere act of moving from left to right becomes a joy in its own right. This tangibility of the controls became the template for whole generations of platformers and still counts as the gold standard today.

The cultural impact is immeasurable. Mario became not only the face of Nintendo but one of the most recognizable fictional characters on the planet, recognizable across continents and generations. The melody from the first level is among the most famous compositions in the history of media. Video games suddenly became mainstream.

Playing Super Mario Bros. today means touching the cornerstone of an entire industry. It is a game that seems simple, yet is perfectly polished, and it is precisely in that simplicity that its immortality lies.

**Why play:** Because it is the game that saved the games industry and defined platformers — timeless, perfectly controllable and still fun.
