Over the years, the game expanded its roster with paid fighters through the Fighters Pass, bringing in completely unexpected faces such as Sephiroth from Final Fantasy VII, Steve from Minecraft, Kazuya from Tekken, or Sora from Kingdom Hearts, and the final fighter roster exceeded ninety characters. Each of them received their own set of moves and animations, which makes Ultimate a project whose scope is unique in the fighting genre.

The core gameplay stays faithful to the series: it's a platform fighter where the goal isn't to zero out an opponent's health bar, but to increase their damage percentage and then knock them off the screen. This simple principle is also the reason the game works on two completely different levels – as chaotic fun for four people on the couch with random items, and as a tightly tuned one-on-one duel without any distracting elements. Ultimate adds an elaborate single-player mode, World of Light, with an expansive challenge map and hundreds of spirits inspired by characters from across the entire games industry, whose traits can be combined into custom builds.

The game also excels as a spectated esports title thanks to its deep movement system and an active community that holds tournaments around the world. The visuals, a soundtrack numbering in the thousands of tracks, and a huge selection of arenas make Ultimate arguably the most comprehensive crossover title in video game history and the flagship of Switch multiplayer. The game's online side, on the other hand, was long a target of criticism for its unstable connection, so the competitive scene made do with its own unofficial solutions for years and tournaments were preferentially played live. Even so, Ultimate remains a game that you just need to turn on, and any group of people instantly knows what to do.

switch__splatoon-2.article:
**Splatoon 2** brought a refreshingly colorful alternative to traditional shooters onto the Switch. Instead of eliminating opponents, the goal is to cover as much territory as possible in your own team's ink, which makes the game a more strategic and accessible experience than classic arenas – even a player who doesn't hit anyone can win the match for their team by diligently painting the floor. Players, in the form of humanoid squid-kids called Inklings, can transform into cephalopods and in this form move lightning-fast through their own color across walls and floors, creating a unique rhythm between attack and tactical maneuvering. Ink serves simultaneously as ammunition and as terrain, so shooting, movement, and territory capture are all one and the same activity in this game.

Besides four-versus-four Turf War matches, the game offers ranked Ranked Battles with variations like Rainmaker or Tower Control, as well as a full-fledged single-player campaign set in the underground Octo Valley, where the Inklings face an army of Octarians; the campaign also serves as an excellent tutorial for controls and the individual weapon types. The off-battlefield layer deserves special attention too: the capital city of Inkopolis Square has its own music industry with idol bands, whose songs accompany the seasonal Splatfests – massive community events where players split into two sides based on their preferred theme and compete for the honor of their team.

The second installment added new weapons, such as the Splat Roller and the Dualies pistols with a dodge roll, and expanded the offering with the cooperative Salmon Run mode, in which four players fend off waves of salmonid monsters and collect their eggs. The paid Octo Expansion then offered a series of very difficult trials and a surprisingly dark story that earned a reputation as the best content in the entire game. Splatoon 2 became one of the pillars of the early Switch library, exceptionally popular especially in Japan, and cemented the series' reputation as the most distinctive new brand Nintendo has created in the last decade.

switch__splatoon-3.article:
**Splatoon 3** moves the action from Inkopolis to the sunny coastal town of Splatsville in the Splatlands region, where Inklings and the newly playable Octolings converge from all around. Visually, it's a shift toward a rougher, desert-like, street-fashion-soaked style that suits the series and sets it apart from its more cleanly colorful predecessors. The core gameplay remains faithful to the series – painting territory in your own color, transforming into a cephalopod for quick movement, and competing in team Turf War matches and ranked modes – but Splatoon 3 adds a new weapon class, the Stringers (ink bows), and the Splatana, wide wiper blades for close combat, noticeably broadening the range of possible playstyles.

Also new is Tricolor Turf War, a three-team match that appears during Splatfests. The single-player campaign, Return of the Mammalians, is the most expansive in the series and tells a darker story about a strange furry entity controlling the inhabitants of the Splatlands, with a visually spectacular finale. The cooperative monster-wave mode Salmon Run, popular from the previous installment, has become a permanent part of the game instead of limited time windows, allowing it to be played anytime, and the collectible card game Tableturf Battle was added, translating the territory-capturing principle onto a board and becoming a surprisingly addictive side pastime.

Splatfests were revised into a three-way clash, pitting three factions against each other instead of two, and the game regularly receives new weapons, maps, and cosmetic items through seasonal updates as well as the paid Side Order expansion, which offers a roguelite challenge with the heroine from Octo Expansion, Agent 8. The developers also gradually improved connection quality and the speed of returning to the game after a match, things the community had long criticized in previous installments. Splatoon 3 became one of the fastest-selling titles in Japan and confirmed that Nintendo managed to build the original brand into a mainstay with a loyal community outside of the traditional Mario and Zelda franchises.

switch__animal-crossing-new-horizons.article:
**Animal Crossing: New Horizons** launched in March 2020, at the exact moment the world got stuck in lockdowns because of the pandemic, and it became an unexpected cultural phenomenon and refuge for millions of players. The game leaves behind the series' established towns and puts the player in the role of the first resident of an uninhabited island, who, with the help of the raccoon-run company Tom Nook, gradually builds it up from scratch – from a tent through their own house to an extensive village full of animal neighbors. Progress isn't driven by experience or levels but by small tasks and mortgage installments, creating a calm, gentle rhythm where nothing is ever on fire.

A key element is real time: the game runs according to the actual date and clock, seasons, holidays, and the day-night cycle all change, which supports a long-term, meditative rhythm of play rather than a chase after a goal. The new terraforming mechanic allows you to change the terrain, build bridges and ladders, and move entire rivers, so every island has a completely unique look reflecting its owner's taste; the community around sharing island designs became its own phenomenon on social media. Gathering fruit, catching fish and bugs for the museum, crafting furniture using DIY recipes, and visiting neighboring islands via Nintendo Switch Online form the core of an endless loop of activities, complemented by the turnip exchange, the one genuinely tense part of the game.

The game also allows for rich creative expression through a clothing and pattern design tool, with which players crafted everything from paving tiles to replicas of designer outfits. Thanks to its soothing atmosphere, gentle acoustic music that changes every hour, cute graphics, and the absence of any pressure to perform, New Horizons became a symbol of the pandemic era and one of the best-selling exclusive Switch titles ever. Subsequent free updates added characters like café owner Brewster or musician K.K. Slider, and the paid Happy Home Paradise expansion added design work on other residents' vacation homes.

switch__super-mario-maker-2.article:
**Super Mario Maker 2** brings to Switch an idea that proved on Wii U just how powerful a tool can arise from simple platforming building blocks. The game gives players the full set of tools Nintendo itself used for decades to build Mario platformers – from the classic Super Mario Bros. style through New Super Mario Bros. to 3D World – and lets them design their own levels by dragging blocks, enemies, and mechanisms directly on the touchscreen. Each style doesn't just change the graphics but also the jump physics and enemy behavior, so the same design plays completely differently in a different style.

New compared to the first game is a nighttime palette that changes the rules of individual worlds, water currents, slopes, linked On/Off switches, and above all a full-fledged Story Mode, in which Mario helps rebuild Princess Peach's castle across more than a hundred hand-designed levels from Nintendo itself – these also serve as an excellent showcase of everything the editor can do. The online community aspect remains the heart of the game: players upload their own creations to a global server, rate them with a thumbs up, work through difficulty leaderboards in Endless Challenge mode, and compete in online multiplayer races across community levels.

The editor is remarkably deep and allows creating not just traditional jumping segments but also complex logic puzzles, auto-scrollers, escape rooms, or music sequencers that exploit the game's physics in ways the developers hardly intended. This layer of ingenuity is exactly what made Mario Maker 2 a phenomenon on streaming platforms, where watching desperate attempts to beat extremely difficult kaizo levels became entertainment in its own right. Thanks to its huge and creative community, the game contains effectively endless content that continues to grow to this day, and it has become a favorite tool for speedrunners and creators of custom minigames built purely from Mario's building blocks.

switch__luigi-s-mansion-3.article:
**Luigi's Mansion 3** puts the timid Luigi in the role of the main hero, who, with the help of the upgraded Poltergust G-00 vacuum, must face an army of ghosts in the luxurious Last Resort hotel, where he was invited on vacation along with Mario, Peach, and friends. The trap was set by the sinister painter King Boo, whose magic portrait pulled the whole group into a trap and turned the hotel into a nest of ghosts scattered across its floors, each of which has its own visual theme – from a kitchen through an art floor to a frozen swimming pool. The hotel's structure is also a clever pacing solution: each floor works as a separate episode with its own puzzle and boss, so the game never turns into repetition.

The gameplay combines exploration and puzzle-solving using a flashlight and vacuum with tense combat sequences against ghosts, which must first be stunned with a flash and then sucked up. New moves were added too, such as a vacuum slam or a burst of exhaust air, giving fights against larger groups of ghosts noticeably better pacing than in previous installments. New is the companion Gooigi, a gelatinous copy of Luigi, who can be controlled by a second player in co-op or switched to solo for solving puzzles that require two characters at once, though Gooigi can pass through grates but is vulnerable to water and sharp objects. The game also offers robust multiplayer modes, ScareScraper and ScreamPark, for up to eight players locally and online.

Visually, it's one of the technically most impressive titles on Switch thanks to detailed animations, playful lighting, soft shadows, and comic-book-like character expressions – Luigi's terrified faces rank among the best things Nintendo's animators have ever shown. Almost every piece of furniture is interactive, so vacuuming curtains, pillows, and trash is entertaining in its own right. Critics praised the humor, the creativity of the boss fights, and the solid length of the campaign, making Luigi's Mansion 3 one of the best-reviewed titles in the series and a favorite choice for players looking for a lighter but visually rich action-adventure.

switch__pokemon-sword-and-shield.article:
**Pokémon Sword and Shield** marked the main Pokémon series' debut on a home console and, at the same time, the first fully 3D open environments in mainline games. The story takes trainers to the Galar region, inspired by Great Britain, where the challenge for the league also becomes a journey full of gym battles taking place in front of a roaring crowd in giant stadiums – enabled by the new Dynamax mechanic, which temporarily enlarges a Pokémon to gigantic proportions and, in even rarer cases, transforms its appearance through Gigantamax. The football-like, sporting atmosphere of the whole league gave the series a new flair: gym battles feel like sold-out matches, complete with fans, uniforms, and anthem-like songs.

The open Wild Area was a novelty for the series: a sprawling meadow full of randomly roaming wild Pokémon and changing weather that affects which species appear, plus a free camera the series hadn't known until then. This is also where cooperative Max Raid Battles are focused, in which four players team up to take on a single giant Pokémon. The game also introduced new Galarian forms of familiar Pokémon adapted to the local environment and expanded the Galar League's roster of trainers with more distinctive personalities, including rival Hop and champion Leon.

The release was accompanied by controversy over the so-called Dexit – for the first time in the series' history, it wasn't possible to transfer all Pokémon from previous generations, which divided the fanbase and sparked debate about how far the series can grow. Even so, the game sold exceptionally well, and two expansions, Isle of Armor and Crown Tundra, added new areas, legendary Pokémon, and characters. Sword and Shield showed where the series could head on more powerful hardware and paved the way for even more open successors. The side mode of cooking curry at the campfire added an unexpectedly beloved pastime, letting players spend time with their team outside of battles.

switch__pokemon-legends-arceus.article:
**Pokémon Legends: Arceus** is the most radical experiment in the history of the mainline Pokémon series. Instead of turn-based battles in the grass and linear towns, it offers a semi-open world set in the distant past of the Hisui region, the predecessor of today's Sinnoh, where the player, as a member of the newly founded Survey Corps, maps unexplored wilderness and compiles the first Pokédex. There's also a crucial shift in tone: at this point in time, people don't yet know Pokémon and are afraid of them, so the game tells a story of discovery and the slow building of trust between two worlds instead of a sporting challenge.

Catching Pokémon happens directly in real time without switching to a separate battle screen – the player sneaks through the landscape, throws Poké Balls at unsuspecting creatures or first weakens them in battle, and a botched attempt can spook an entire herd. Additionally, aggressive Pokémon can now attack the player directly, who can then faint and lose some of the items they've collected, adding unusual tension to exploration. The battles themselves remain turn-based, but sped up and supplemented with new Strong and Agile attack styles that change the turn order and damage amount, so even familiar moves are used differently than before.

The world is divided into several vast areas with different biomes, from volcanic plains to snowy mountains, and the player returns between them to the central Jubilife Village, where gear upgrades and missions for the local residents take place. A special chapter belongs to the so-called noble Pokémon, giant enraged creatures the player faces in action battles involving dodging and throwing healing balms. The story escalates with a darker twist involving the mythological Pokémon Arceus, the creator of the universe. Critics praised Game Freak's courage in abandoning decades-old series conventions, despite technical shortcomings in the form of simpler graphics and occasional frame-rate drops. Legends: Arceus became one of the fastest-selling Pokémon games in history and hinted at the direction the series might take next.

switch__pokemon-scarlet-and-violet.article:
**Pokémon Scarlet and Violet** gave the series its first truly seamless open world without loading screens between locations, set in the Paldea region inspired by Spain and Portugal. The player, as a student at Naranja or Uva Academy, can freely roam the landscape in any direction from the opening hours and follow three parallel storylines at once – the traditional challenge of eight gyms, a fight against the criminal organization Team Star made up of bullied school outsiders, and tracking down a legendary Pokémon, whether the fiery Koraidon or the electric Miraidon, which also serves as a riding companion enabling gliding, swimming, and wall-climbing. Because the game doesn't scale difficulty according to progress, one of its strongest moments comes when the player accidentally heads into an area they're nowhere near ready for.

This open approach was a crucial step for the series following the partially open experiment of Legends: Arceus, although the release was accompanied by significant technical criticism due to frame-rate drops, graphical glitches, and engine instability, sparking one of the sharpest discussions about the quality of a mainline entry in the series' history. The contrast between the ambition of the design and the state in which the game launched is arguably the project's biggest weakness, even though later updates eased many of the issues.

Still, the game offered popular novelties like the cooperative Tera Raid Battles, using the crystalline typing system of Terastallization, which temporarily changes a Pokémon's type and resistances, fundamentally transforming competitive play as well – suddenly you couldn't guess an opponent's weaknesses just by looking at them. It's also possible to explore the entire world together with three friends. Two expansions, The Teal Mask and The Indigo Disk, expanded the story with additional regions and legendary Pokémon while also offering the toughest battles in the game. Despite the technical issues, Scarlet and Violet became the commercially most successful games in the series ever, and their story about searching for one's own treasure ranks among the best-written the series has ever had.

switch__fire-emblem-three-houses.article:
**Fire Emblem: Three Houses** combines the series' tactical turn-based battles with a school-life simulation at the monastery academy of Garreg Mach, where the player, in the role of professor Byleth, takes charge of one of three student houses – the Blue Lions, the Black Eagles, or the Golden Deer, each representing a different faction of the continent of Fódlan. The game's structure follows a calendar: each month has its own preparation phase and ends with a mandatory mission, so the player must constantly choose what to spend their limited time on, including deciding which students to try to recruit into their own house.

Off the battlefield, the player spends time teaching subjects, building relationships with students through conversations and tea parties, fishing, cooking, and developing their own and their students' skills, which directly affects their combat abilities and the possibility of advancing to higher classes. The class system is significantly more flexible than in older installments – almost any character can head down almost any path if the player devotes enough teaching to them. The battles themselves stay true to the series – permanent unit death, a rock-paper-scissors duel between weapon types, and expansive maps with terrain advantages – but they're enriched by magical Combat Arts, calling in reinforcement squads, and the ability to command your own professor as a full-fledged combat unit. For less patient players, there's also a turn-rewind mode available.

A crucial element is the political story: midway through the game, a large-scale war breaks out between the three factions, and the choice of house from the first half of the game fundamentally changes the narrative, allies, and enemies in the second part, giving the game enormous replayability and leading to beloved students from the first playthrough appearing as enemies in the second. The Cindered Shadows expansion added a fourth hidden faction. Thanks to the depth of its characters, the moral ambiguity of the factions, and its elaborate relationship system, Three Houses is considered one of the most ambitious and best-written installments in the entire series, and also a title that opened the series to an entirely new audience.

switch__xenoblade-chronicles-2.article:
**Xenoblade Chronicles 2** places the player in the world of Alrest, where humanity survives on the backs of giant living Titans sailing an endless sea of clouds, since dry land vanished long ago. The main hero Rex, a salvager diving to the bottom of this sea, accidentally awakens the mysterious Pyra, one of the legendary Blades – living weapons in the form of companions, who bond with humans called Drivers and lend them extraordinary abilities. Together they set out to find the mythical World Tree on the back of the Titan Architect, in exchange for which Pyra promises to grant Rex's wish.

The combat system builds on the fluid connection between characters and their Blades, elemental combo effects, and strategic on-the-fly weapon switching, making it one of the more complex combat systems in the genre; its high point is several-minute-long chain combos, during which elemental orbs gradually build up on screen and the player finally lets them all explode at once. Mastering it takes a while, though, because the game explains its layers gradually and somewhat unsystematically, which was the most common criticism from reviewers. Blades are also obtained by randomly opening crystals, a mechanic that split players into two camps.

The world is divided into several giant Titans, each functioning as a separate open region with its own culture, fauna, and side quests, and the player can easily spend hundreds of hours exploring its nooks, hidden treasures, and collectibles. Visually, the game relies on anime stylization and monumental vistas, albeit at the cost of a softer resolution in handheld mode. The soundtrack, led by a team including Yasunori Mitsuda and Manaka Kataoka, ranks among the most praised in the genre. The Torna: The Golden Country expansion then functions as a standalone game telling a prequel story set long before the main storyline. Thanks to its expansive world, emotional storytelling, and inventive Blades system, Xenoblade Chronicles 2 became one of the pillars of the JRPG genre on Switch.

switch__xenoblade-chronicles-3.article:
**Xenoblade Chronicles 3** merges the worlds of the previous two games – Bionis and Alrest – into a single continent, Aionios, split between two warring nations, Keves and Agnus, whose inhabitants live a short life predetermined from birth, ended by the Homecoming ritual the moment they reach adulthood. The main group of six heroes, three from each side, meet in the middle of a battle and, thanks to a mystical power, merge into what's called Ouroboros, a powerful fusion form that transcends the boundary between the warring nations, beginning their shared search for the truth about who is really behind the endless war.

The combat system builds on the mechanics of both previous installments, combining battlefield positioning, Chain Attacks, and tactical party roles similar to classes from MMOs, such as tank, healer, or damage dealer, with the ability to switch party members' classes on the fly. The party is also the largest in the series – seven characters at once, including temporary guests – and switching to Ouroboros form mid-battle serves as a powerful trump card with its own attacks and its own risk of overheating. The world of Aionios is vast and seamless, dotted with strongholds called Colonies, which the player gradually liberates and expands with new inhabitants, equipment, and side stories that rank among the best-written in the entire series.

The narrative is among the darkest and most philosophically demanding in the series, dealing with themes of death, the meaning of a short life, and the cycle of endless conflict, though unlike its predecessors it's delivered in a more sober tone with significantly fewer anime clichés. The Future Redeemed expansion offers an epilogue that brings together characters from all three games and also brings back Shulk and Rex. Critics praised Xenoblade Chronicles 3 as the most emotionally powerful and complex entry in the series, though also the most demanding to understand without knowledge of the previous two installments, and at the same time as one of the technically most ambitious titles ever released on Switch.

switch__metroid-dread.article:
**Metroid Dread** is the first entirely new two-dimensional entry in the series in nineteen years, created through a collaboration between Nintendo and the Spanish studio MercurySteam, which had previously made the Samus Returns remake. The game picks up directly after the events of Metroid Fusion, sending bounty hunter Samus Aran to the planet ZDR to investigate a mysterious signal suggesting the presence of the X parasite, believed to have been eradicated. Samus soon finds herself stripped of most of her equipment inside a sealed underground complex crawling with hostile robots called E.M.M.I., which cannot be fought in the early stages of the game -- the only option is to run, hide, and search for an escape hatch, or face instant death.

It is precisely the E.M.M.I.-guarded zones that give the game its rhythm. The map is split into regular areas and sealed sectors where the robot roams freely, reacts to the sound of footsteps, and launches a relentless chase the moment it spots Samus, with the only way out being a door on the far side of the block. This tension mechanic gave the game its very name and returns the series to a sense of vulnerability that had long been missing. Gradually unlocking abilities such as the Morph Ball, various beam types, or the teleporting Phantom Cloak opens up previously inaccessible parts of the map in the classic metroidvania style the series is named after. The combat system is enriched by a new counterattack mechanic, the Melee Counter, allowing a lightning-fast response to an enemy attack, and Samus's overall movement is unusually fast -- slides, sprints, and omnidirectional aiming flow into one another almost without any delay.

The visuals and animation fluidity rank among the best the series has ever offered. The environments of ZDR alternate between cold industrial complexes, flooded caverns, and scorching magma shafts, and the music leans on atmospheric undertones and silence rather than pronounced melodies, which only underscores the feeling of isolation in a hostile underground world. Dread was received by critics and fans alike as a triumphant return and one of the finest conclusions to Samus Aran's long-running story arc. Today it stands as a convincing proof that the classic two-dimensional format doesn't need to be modernized at any cost -- it just needs to be honed to absolute technical perfection.

switch__kirby-and-forgotten-land.article:
**Kirby and the Forgotten Land** represents the first genuinely three-dimensional open level design in the history of the Kirby series, even though it remains more of a semi-linear corridor than a free sandbox -- the player moves through the remnants of an abandoned human civilization, overgrown with nature and transformed into a post-apocalyptic playground full of shopping malls, amusement parks, and crumbling roads. After a mysterious storm, Kirby is separated from his home planet, Popstar, and swept into this new world, where he must rescue the kidnapped Waddle Dees from the clutches of the animalistic Beast Army.

The classic abilities of inhaling and copying enemy powers remain the core of the game, but the new addition is Mouthful Mode, in which Kirby can swallow giant objects such as a car, a traffic cone, or a vending machine to gain entirely new, situational abilities for solving puzzles and fights. Copied abilities can also be upgraded in the village using collected resources, so what starts as a simple arsenal gradually becomes a surprisingly varied toolkit. The level design is split into smaller, self-contained stages linked by an exploration map, with side objectives centered on rescuing captured Waddle Dees, who then populate and expand the central Waddle Dee Town with shops and minigames. The game also offers a cooperative mode for a second player controlling the helper Bandana Waddle Dee, making the playthrough accessible even to a pair with markedly different experience levels.

After completing the main campaign, a tougher epilogue called Isolated Isles awaits, with boss fights pushing the series' difficulty to its limits and turning what was initially an undemanding game into a solid challenge. Visually it is one of the best-looking titles in the series -- the contrast between Kirby's pastel cuteness and the quiet, overgrown, people-less civilization creates an unexpectedly melancholic undertone, complemented by a sweeping soundtrack that mixes orchestral and rock arrangements. Forgotten Land became the best-selling Kirby title in history, and critics praised especially its unexpectedly emotional and atmospheric tone. Today it is regarded as the point where the series finally and convincingly nailed the transition into three dimensions.

switch__super-mario-bros-wonder.article:
**Super Mario Bros. Wonder** is the first entirely new two-dimensional Mario title in over a decade of stagnation under the New Super Mario Bros. label, and it returned to the series the creativity that sub-brand had gradually been losing. The central element of every level is the mysterious Wonder Flower, which upon collection radically disrupts the rules of physics and transforms the environment -- pipes suddenly come alive and crawl through the entire level, Mario turns into a giant snake made of blocks, gravity flips upside down, or the whole scene dissolves into a stylized, hand-painted sequence. This unpredictability turns every level into a small surprise, a major departure from the formula of previous entries.

The game also introduces new powers such as the Elephant Fruit, turning Mario and friends into trunked elephants able to sweep away enemies with their trunk or scoop up water, and the Bubble Flower, which creates bubbles that serve as both platforms and weapons. A second layer of customization comes from badges, which permanently alter movement -- from gliding and sticky gloves to deliberately harder variants for those seeking a challenge. The visual style moves away from the geometric cleanliness of the New Super Mario Bros. series in favor of more expressive animations and character expressions, which for the first time in the series' history genuinely react to their surroundings with sounds and grimaces. A whole roster of characters is playable as well, including Yoshi and Nabbit in an easier, damage-free mode, so a mixed family group can easily gather around a single game.

Cooperative play is also supported by an online mode in which shadows of other players move through the level and can revive one another without getting in each other's way. Wonder was received by critics as a return to the experimental playfulness of classic Mario titles and one of the best-reviewed platformers of the entire generation, with reviewers particularly praising its willingness to break its own established rules in nearly every level. The game became one of the best-selling titles of the Switch's twilight years and still stands today as proof that two-dimensional Mario has plenty left to offer, given room for ideas instead of repeating a template.

switch__bayonetta-3.article:
**Bayonetta 3** closes out the long-awaited trilogy of the stylish action series about a witch fighting both angelic and demonic forces, this time on a far more cosmic scale -- the multiverse is under attack from an entity called Homunculus, destroying parallel worlds one by one, and Bayonetta must team up with alternate versions of herself to prevent the destruction of her own reality as well. Visually, the game travels across exotic locations from Chinese mountains to Tokyo streets and decaying alternate realities, giving the story a grand, genre-crossing tone.

The core of the combat system stays true to the series' trademark lightning-fast dodge, Witch Time, which slows time on a perfect evasion and opens a window for a devastating combo, but the game adds giant summonable Demon forms -- monstrous shapes Bayonetta temporarily transforms into, letting her wreck entire city streets and take on giant enemies at a kaiju scale reminiscent of Japanese monster movies. Controlling the Demon forms happens alongside controlling her own character, so the player must keep an eye on two bodies at once and find the right moment to safely shift focus. A newcomer to the roster of playable characters is the younger Bayonetta, named Viola, armed with a sword and her own demonic companion, with a different, more aggressive fighting style than the title heroine -- instead of dodging, she relies on precisely timed blocking, demanding a different rhythm and different habits.

Like the rest of the series, Bayonetta 3 is aimed squarely at an adult audience due to its violence, sexualized stylized character design, and dark themes; for more sensitive players it also offers an optional mode that tones down the most explicit elements. Technically it is one of the most ambitious titles on Switch, attempting massive set-piece scenes at the cost of occasional compromises in resolution and frame rate. Critics praised the boldness of the boss fights and the sheer scope of content, though the story and ending divided fans of the series with its exposition and the controversial resolution of the title heroine's fate. Today Bayonetta 3 is seen as a divisive but unmissable conclusion to one of the most distinctive action franchises around.

switch__astral-chain.article:
**Astral Chain** is an original exclusive title from PlatinumGames under the creative direction of Takahisa Taura, writer of NieR: Automata, set in the near future, where humanity has relocated its last remaining metropolis onto an artificial island after Earth was invaded by extradimensional monsters called Chimeras. The player takes on the role of an officer in the special unit Neuron, equipped with the ability to summon and control their own Legion -- a tamed Chimera tethered by an invisible astral chain that can be controlled in combat alongside the player's own character.

This dual control is the heart of the combat system: the player maneuvers their detective on the front line while simultaneously using the chain to steer their Legion, catching enemies, creating barriers, or performing synchronized combo attacks, with five Legion types offering distinct fighting styles ranging from a sword and a firearm to transforming into a motorcycle for chases. The chain itself also serves as a tool -- it can be wrapped around an enemy, used to pull yourself toward it, or stretched across an enemy's attack path as a trap, turning combat into more of a positional spatial game than simple button-mashing. Outside of combat, the game also functions as a detective adventure -- the player investigates cases around the city, collects evidence, interviews witnesses, helps civilians, and decides how to allocate Neuron unit resources, which affects the side content. Each chapter also closes with a performance rating that encourages a cleaner repeat playthrough.

The visual style combines cyberpunk aesthetics with colorful, almost anime-style stylization of the combat, and the contrast between the island's sterile streets and the warped astral plane ranks among the strongest imagery of the entire generation. The controls are demanding on coordination at first, and the game requires several hours before dual-managing the character and the Legion feels natural in the player's hands, but the satisfaction once combat clicks is all the greater for it. Astral Chain was received by critics as one of the most original new titles of the generation and a showcase of how PlatinumGames can experiment even outside its established franchises.

switch__donkey-kong-country-tropical-fre.article:
**Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze** originally released on Wii U in 2014 and arrived on Switch in a reworked version four years later, finally finding the audience it deserved. It is one of the most demanding and visually accomplished 2D platformers of the generation: an icy army called the Snowmads invades Donkey Kong's island and turns his tropical home into a frozen wasteland, forcing the gorilla and his friends to journey back across the island and drive the Snowmads out.

The gameplay is built on precise controls where every jump, roll, and vine grab has to land pixel-perfect, and the level design full of waterfall sequences, tornadoes, and vertically climbing passages ranks among the most inventive in the genre. The camera often sweeps across the whole scene and uses foreground and background as part of the action, so the levels feel spatial even though the game is played strictly in two dimensions. Diddy Kong, Dixie Kong, and newcomer Cranky Kong act as riding companions strapped to Donkey's back, each offering a unique ability -- Dixie slows the fall with a helicopter spin from her ponytail, Cranky can bounce his cane over dangerous terrain like thorns or poison water, and Diddy adds a short jetpack flight. The choice of companion fundamentally changes how individual passages can be approached, and collectibles hidden off the main path reward exploration.

Boss fights against the captains of the Snowmad fleet rank among the most visually spectacular in the series, and the music by David Wise, a veteran of the original SNES trilogy, was repeatedly praised by critics as one of the best video game soundtracks of the decade, especially the underwater tracks that echo classic themes from the nineties. The Switch version added a simpler New Funky Mode for less experienced players, giving Funky Kong extra lives and abilities and significantly lowering the entry barrier. Tropical Freeze is still considered one of the best-crafted 2D platformers on the market and a title that deservedly found a second life well beyond the underperforming Wii U.

switch__mario-rabbids-kingdom-battle.article:
**Mario + Rabbids Kingdom Battle** sounded like a bizarre idea on paper -- combining the Mario universe with the chaotic Rabbids from Ubisoft -- but the resulting turn-based tactical shooter surprised everyone with production quality comparable to genre classics like XCOM. Thanks to a mysterious device called SupaMerge, the Rabbids are accidentally transported into Mario's Mushroom Kingdom and inadvertently merge it with their own reality, creating a warped, glitch-riddled world in which Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Yoshi must team up with heroic Rabbid copies of themselves to face the chaos the other Rabbids have caused.

The combat system combines cover, grid-based movement, and firearms with classic Mario abilities such as jumping off a teammate's head to reach farther positions, or character-specific special attacks, with each hero-Rabbid pair offering a distinct combination of weapons and abilities. Crucially, movement, a sliding attack into an enemy, and a jump all happen within a single turn without spending an action, turning every round into a small puzzle sequence focused on finding the most efficient route across the map. The level design gradually introduces new mechanics, from simple skirmishes to complex puzzles using terrain and environmental traps, and between battles the player walks through a lightly stylized world with simple puzzles of its own.

The game's humor, full of absurd gags and parodies of the Mario universe, stays true to the Rabbids' style, but the elaborate tactical layer elevates it well above mere parody, aided by an orchestral soundtrack that plays with Mario themes with a knowing wink. The game's design was led by Italian game designer Davide Soliani, whose passion for the project helped convince Nintendo itself to collaborate, one of the most surprising moves by the Japanese company at the time of its announcement. The game also received the Donkey Kong Adventure expansion and a full-fledged sequel, Sparks of Hope, in 2022, and remains one of the most pleasant entry points into turn-based tactics.

switch__ring-fit-adventure.article:
**Ring Fit Adventure** combines the fitness game genre with a light RPG adventure and managed to win over even players who had long been skeptical of exercise-focused titles. The game ships with unique hardware accessories -- a flexible ring called the Ring-Con, into which one Joy-Con controller slots, and a leg strap for the other -- which use these to sense squeezing, pulling, and squats, so the player's real physical movement directly controls the in-game character. The Ring-Con itself is purely mechanical with no electronics, and all the sensing is handled by the sensors inside the controllers.

The story is a lighthearted excuse for a string of exercise minigames: the evil dragon Dragaux has stolen the region's freedom, and the player's character, together with a talking ring named Ring, must run through dozens of worlds, gathering experience, treasure, and leveling up stats like in a classic RPG. Individual levels combine running in place across a map, battles against enemies resolved with specific exercises tied to attack types such as ab, yoga, or strength moves, and short minigames testing balance or reaction speed. Because each exercise has its own color and enemies have varying resistance to each color, a subtle tactical layer emerges that naturally pushes the player to alternate muscle groups instead of repeating a single favorite move. The game tracks heart rate if the player connects a compatible watch, and lets them adjust workout intensity to their own fitness level, from a light warm-up to a genuinely demanding, adrenaline-pumping session.

Due to gym closures during the pandemic, Ring Fit Adventure became one of the most sought-after and long sold-out titles on the market, proving that gaming can serve as a legitimate form of home exercise. The game also includes standalone quick workout sets outside the adventure mode for players who just want a short daily session without following the story, plus a quiet mode with exercises that don't require stomping for apartment living. Today Ring Fit is regarded as the most convincing attempt at gamifying exercise any major publisher has ever undertaken.

switch__1-2-switch.article:
**1-2-Switch** was one of the console's launch titles and had a single goal -- to show at a glance what the Joy-Con controllers could do, without players even needing to watch the TV screen. A collection of nearly thirty minigames, such as a quick-draw cowboy shootout, milking a virtual cow, simulating hand-washing, or guessing the number of coins in a hand, is played primarily according to instructions shown on screen, while the actual players look at each other and rely on the haptic feedback of HD Rumble and the controllers' motion sensors.

It is precisely this social aspect, where the screen becomes largely irrelevant and the game plays out between the people in the room, that was meant to demonstrate the console's portability and flexibility in the spirit of classic party games like Wii Sports. The best events are the ones built around subtle vibrations -- for example, guessing the number of marbles inside a virtual box, where the player slowly tilts the controller and judges the count purely by the feel in their palm. This is exactly where HD Rumble showed what it was really good for, since no earlier console could grade feedback with such nuance. The other minigames, however, stick to simple motions and wear thin after a few rounds, so the game lives and dies by the mood of the group playing it.

Critics received the game with mixed feelings due to the shallow depth of individual minigames, the lack of single-player content, and a fairly high price relative to the amount of fun on offer, but as a social showcase of the technology at family gatherings it found its audience and sold surprisingly well in the console's first months. Over time, Nintendo dusted off the concept in related titles like Nintendo Switch Sports, which offered a similar motion-control philosophy in a more sporty and accessible package. Today, 1-2-Switch feels more like a technological calling card for the Joy-Cons' capabilities than a full-fledged gaming experience, but it fulfilled its role in introducing the console.

switch__arms.article:
**ARMS** is an original fighting series from Nintendo in which characters are equipped with extremely stretchy spring-loaded arms that let them strike opponents from a distance, dodge, block, and chain hits into more complex combos. The game is controlled primarily through motion -- the player physically punches with the Joy-Cons in hand, twisting them to curve the punch's flight path around obstacles or an opponent's guard, although traditional button controls are also available for players who prefer a classic approach.

Unlike most fighting games, ARMS takes place in an open three-dimensional space, so alongside timing, positioning, distance, and the angle a punch arrives from all come into play -- a match feels more like long-range fencing than a classic brawler. The roster offers over ten distinctive fighters, from the mechanical girl Ribbon Girl through the fiery chef Master Mummy to the robot Springtron, with each character differing in height, speed, and specific arms carrying their own traits such as electric shock, fire, or freezing, which the player can freely mix and match before a match. The arenas and game modes are varied, from classic one-on-one duels through bomb volleyball to a basketball mode where the goal is to dunk the opponent into a hoop, and the arenas also feature obstacles and moving platforms that change the flow of combat.

Nintendo supported the game long-term after release with free updates adding new fighters, arenas, and game modes, turning it into a living title with an active, if smaller, community, and the game also received regular online tournament events. Visually it is one of the cleanest-looking titles on Switch, with bold colors and smooth performance that players who play at a fast pace will especially appreciate. Critics praised the originality of the concept and the depth of the combat system, though some players noted the game lacks single-player content and a broader story context. ARMS remains one of the few entirely new franchises Nintendo introduced during the Switch generation.

switch__captain-toad-treasure-tracker.article:
**Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker** grew out of the minigames that appeared in Super Mario 3D World and expands them into a full-fledged puzzle platformer in which the jump-incapable titular Toad moves through compact diorama levels shaped like cubes, towers, and intricate structures that can be freely rotated and viewed from every angle so the player can uncover hidden paths, keys, and treasures. Each level fits on a single screen and feels like a miniature model the player peers into from various sides.

Without the ability to jump, Toad must rely on clever maneuvering, collecting stars, avoiding enemies such as poisonous Piranha Plants or giant Wigglers, and the occasional use of special items like a mining pick or a turnip-throwing weapon against the boss Wingo, a bird who stole the treasure as well as Toad's companion, Toadette. The lack of a jump isn't a deprivation but the main design rule -- it forces the player to think the route through ahead of time, since a wrong step often means backtracking across the entire structure. The Switch version added new levels inspired by Super Mario Odyssey, a cooperative mode for a second player controlling a companion character, and gyroscope motion-control support for precisely aiming at hidden objects.

The design of individual levels emphasizes spatial reasoning and observation over reflexes, setting the game apart from most Mario-led platformers, and each level also contains three hidden gems and a secret collectible goal revealed only after the first completion. Short but dense levels and a welcoming difficulty make Treasure Tracker a beloved choice for family play as well as for players seeking a relaxing alternative to more demanding platformers, and the format of one level lasting just a few minutes suits handheld play perfectly. Critics praised the game for its inventive level design and charm, although some faulted its overall lower difficulty and length.

switch__new-super-mario-bros-u-deluxe.article:
**New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe** is a Switch compilation of the 2012 Wii U game along with its expansion New Super Luigi U, offering shorter and harder versions of the same levels with Luigi as the playable character. The base game sticks to the tried-and-tested formula of classic 2D Mario platformers -- Bowser has once again kidnapped Princess Peach, and Mario and friends make their way through a series of themed worlds ranging from grassy plains through deserts to icy kingdoms, collecting coins, star coins, and bonus items like the Super Acorn, which grants a brief flight.

The Switch version added the new playable Toadette, who transforms into the powerful Peachette after collecting a Super Crown and gains her own abilities, and offers a slightly gentler difficulty for newer players thanks to Nabbit, a damage-immune companion. The game's structure rests on a connected world map with branching paths, hidden exits, and towers, so even a linear progression leaves room to search for secret routes. The game supports up to four players locally in a chaotic cooperative mode, where cooperation easily tips into comic frustration as characters collide with or knock each other off the screen; the Deluxe version, however, keeps groups with children together more easily thanks to damage-immune characters and bubble revival.

Although it is more of a solid, competently crafted platformer without major innovations over earlier entries in the series, its accessibility, compact length, and affordable price made it a popular choice for families with children and for players seeking an undemanding yet well-crafted platforming experience both on the go and on the TV. The included New Super Luigi U also offers more experienced players a considerably steeper challenge thanks to Luigi's higher jump and the shortened time limits on individual levels, turning each of them into a brief, intense test of precision. In hindsight, Deluxe closes out the New Super Mario Bros. era -- cleanly, reliably, and without any ambition to surprise, something only Super Mario Bros. Wonder would remedy a few years later.

switch__super-mario-3d-world-bowser-s-fu.article:
**Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury** is a Switch package combining a remaster of the beloved Wii U platformer with an entirely new, compact open-world addition. The base game combines the structure of classic linear levels with three-dimensional movement and, as the first entry in the series, allows up to four players to play simultaneously as Mario, Luigi, Peach and cat-suited Toadette, with the key new feature being the Cat Suit, giving characters the ability to climb walls and attack with claws. The levels draw inspiration from previous 2D and 3D entries and offer a variety of mechanics from piano platforms to gravity balls. The Switch version also noticeably sped up character movement and added online co-op.

Bowser's Fury is a standalone adventure where dark energy transforms Bowser into a giant, furious Fury Bowser terrorizing the open island of Lake Lapcat. Mario here teams up with Bowser's son, Bowser Jr., who can be controlled by a second player, collects Cat Shines scattered across the island, and at regular intervals must face the giant Fury Bowser in battles reminiscent of kaiju films, where Mario temporarily grows to a similar size thanks to the Giga Bell. The whole island is a single continuous area with no loading, and the collected Cat Shines gradually change the water level and accessibility of individual areas, so the world transforms along with the player's progress.

This addition is much freer and more experimental than the main game and hinted at the direction Super Mario Odyssey, and the more open approach of the series in general, would later take. It's also an interesting technical experiment - Fury Bowser's incursions flood the scene with rain and red lighting and take place right in the middle of ordinary exploration, without a transition screen. The combination of a polished classic and an imaginative bonus made the package one of the best-reviewed platform titles on Switch, and many reviewers even called the shorter Bowser's Fury a more interesting and daring experience than the main game itself.

switch__pikmin-3-deluxe.article:
**Pikmin 3 Deluxe** is an expanded version of the 2013 Wii U strategy game in which three space explorers from the planet Koppai - Captain Charlie, Alph and Brittany - land on the mysterious planet PNF-404 to save their home planet from famine by gathering enough fruit. The planet strikingly resembles an abandoned Earth seen from the perspective of a creature only a few centimeters tall, so ordinary water droplets, leaves or cans feel like monumental obstacles.

The series' key element remains commanding armies of tiny plant-like creatures called Pikmin, which come in colored types with unique abilities - red ones are fire-resistant, blue ones can breathe underwater, yellow ones conduct electricity and can be thrown higher, and the newly introduced rock and flying Pikmin add further strategic options for solving environmental puzzles and fighting the planet's hostile fauna. The player must efficiently divide time between three playable captains, planning routes to gather enough resources before nightfall, when nocturnal predators devour abandoned Pikmin, creating the tense time management typical of the whole series. Fruit supplies are also converted into days of survival for the crew, so even an inefficient afternoon shows up in the expedition's remaining time.

The Switch version adds new missions featuring Olimar and Louie from the earlier entry, a cooperative story mode for two players, a Bingo Battle competition for collecting specific objects, and the option to control the game by pointing with the Joy-Con, similar to the original Wii U GamePad. It also brought minor simplifications and hints that make the series more accessible to newcomers who previously gave up under the harsh time pressure. Thanks to its unique blend of strategy, time management and adorable visuals accompanied by a quiet, natural soundscape, Pikmin 3 Deluxe remains an accessible entry point into one of Nintendo's most distinctive series.

switch__hollow-knight.article:
**Hollow Knight** is an independent metroidvania from the small Australian studio Team Cherry, whose scope, atmosphere and depth put many big-budget titles to shame. The player controls a nameless insect knight who descends into the vast underground kingdom of Hallownest, once a thriving insect civilization now plagued by a mysterious disease called the Infection, which drives its inhabitants mad and kills them. The story is almost never told directly - it's assembled from fragments of dialogue, inscriptions and environment, so the player largely pieces it together themselves.

Exploring the intertwined caves, catacombs and forgotten cities follows the traditional metroidvania style - new abilities like a double jump, wall jump or the ability to swim in acid gradually open up previously inaccessible areas of a huge, interconnected map, which the player records by hand using purchasable maps from the cartographer. This very delay in mapping is essential: in an unknown area, the player moves blindly for a while, which intensifies the feeling of genuine discovery. The combat system is surprisingly demanding and precise, with dozens of unique bosses, some of which rank among the hardest in the entire genre, and the Charms system allows customizing the main character's passive abilities according to preferred playstyle. After death, a shadow remains at the spot, which must be revisited to recover lost money and full mana capacity.

The visual style with hand-drawn art design and melancholic, orchestral music by Christopher Larkin creates a unique, almost gothic atmosphere of a crumbling kingdom, in which muted colors and quiet passages without music work just as powerfully as the big battles. The game also offers an enormous amount of optional content and secrets, as well as several free expansions, which led to it becoming synonymous with depth and generosity in independent production. Hollow Knight is still considered one of the best metroidvanias ever, and its long-delayed sequel Silksong ranks among the most anticipated indie games in history.

switch__hades.article:
**Hades** is an action roguelike from Supergiant Games, in which the player, as Zagreus, son of the god of the underworld Hades, repeatedly tries to escape the underworld to Olympus, with each failed attempt and subsequent death being fully integrated into the story rather than just a game penalty. During his escape, Zagreus fights his way through four distinct areas of Greek mythology inspired by regions of the underworld, aided in his upgrades by boons from the gods of Olympus like Zeus, Athena or Ares, who offer random combinations of abilities that change the style of each run - from chain lightning through bouncing projectiles to devastating critical hits.

The combat system is fast and readable: a basic attack, a special attack, a dodge and a thrown item are enough to build very different strategies from a combination of six distinct weapons ranging from a sword to a bow to a shield. The key innovation is a sophisticated narrative system: characters remember Zagreus's previous attempts, comment on his failures, and the story develops smoothly with each further run, turning the repeated dying typical of the genre into a meaningful part of the storytelling rather than a frustrating necessity. The sheer amount of voiced dialogue is enormous, so even after dozens of runs the game offers new conversations.

The visual style combines hand-drawn characters with a dark yet colorful stylization of Greek mythology, and Darren Korb's music gives the game a distinctive rock edge that turns into one of the most memorable game soundtracks of the generation during key battles. The system of permanent upgrades using the Darkness currency and relationships with characters motivates repeated playthroughs even after completing the main storyline, which is further supplemented by optional difficulty increases for those who want to go further. Hades collected an unprecedented number of Game of the Year awards across game criticism and is now considered one of the defining titles of the roguelike genre.

switch__stardew-valley.article:
**Stardew Valley** is a phenomenon of the independent scene, programmed, drawn and composed entirely by a single person - Eric Barone, going by the name ConcernedApe. The player inherits a rundown farm from their grandfather and leaves the corporate town of Joja Corporation for the peaceful Pelican Town valley, where they gradually restore fields, grow crops, raise animals, fish, mine in caves full of enemies, and build relationships with a colorful community of villagers, some of whom can even be courted and eventually married.

The game is openly inspired by the Japanese Harvest Moon series, but expands it with much deeper RPG elements, combat in randomized mines, a timing-based fishing minigame, and an extensive crafting system for building structures, tools and machines for processing raw materials. Each day has limited energy and length, so playing relies on small-scale planning - what else to get done before dark, what to invest money in, and when it pays off to process the harvest into a more expensive product instead of selling it directly. A real calendar with seasons affects what crops can be grown and what festivals take place in town, giving the game a natural, meditative rhythm. Villagers have their own daily schedules, birthdays and gradually revealed personal stories, which makes the valley feel inhabited even after dozens of hours.

Huge replayability also stems from the many ways the game can be played - from purely farming-focused to a community project of restoring the abandoned Community Center to competing with the corporate Joja Mart, with several farm types available that favor different playstyles. Pixel visuals and a calm soundtrack that changes with the season make playing more of a relaxing ritual than a challenge. Barone continues to update the game for free with new content, most recently with the extensive 1.6 update featuring new crops and locations. Stardew Valley remains to this day a symbol of what a single dedicated creator can achieve.

switch__celeste.article:
**Celeste** is a precise platformer from the Canadian studio Maddy Makes Games, which beneath the surface of extremely demanding challenges hides a sensitive story about anxiety, depression and self-acceptance. The main heroine Madeline decides to climb the mythical Mount Celeste, and along her journey a dark version of herself gradually materializes, representing the inner anxieties and doubts she must come to terms with. Climbing the mountain thus functions as both a literal and figurative trial, and the side characters Madeline meets along the way hold up a mirror to her.

The gameplay is built on perfectly tuned movement - jumping, an aerial dash in a chosen direction, and wall climbing - with the level design offering hundreds of short, deadly difficult screens requiring pixel-perfect precision, but thanks to instant respawn with no loading it never feels frustrating. Each chapter also introduces its own mechanic, from moving blocks to wind currents to mirror reflections, so the game constantly reinvents itself without abandoning its core movement vocabulary. The game also includes optional, extremely demanding B-Side and C-Side levels for players craving an even bigger challenge, and hidden strawberries scattered across the mountain for collectors. It also includes a detailed assist mode that lets players adjust game speed or the number of dashes without any judgment - accessibility is deliberately part of the design here.

The pixel art visuals combined with Lena Raine's emotive piano music, later acclaimed even outside the gaming community, create a distinctive atmosphere in which the music adapts to what's happening on screen. It's precisely this open treatment of mental health, without simplification or cliché, that earned extraordinary acclaim from critics and players who could personally identify with Madeline's story. Celeste is today considered one of the best-written and, at the same time, best-playing indie platformers ever, despite - or because of - its difficulty.

switch__dead-cells.article:
**Dead Cells** combines the metroidvania genre with a roguelike structure of repeated runs, in which the player controls a formless, immortal entity animating a headless body, moving through a procedurally generated island full of prisons, catacombs and castle chambers. Each attempt starts from scratch with no equipment, but thanks to collected gold cells, players can permanently unlock new weapons, abilities and mutations between runs, gradually expanding the range of possible builds and strategies for future attempts.

The combat system is fast, precise and rewards an aggressive yet thoughtful playstyle combining swords, crossbows, grenades, traps and magic runes, with combinations of weapons and mutations allowing the construction of hundreds of different builds, from a silent assassin to a fiery berserker. Weapons are divided by three stats that also boost health, so choosing your equipment fundamentally changes not just your attack but also your survivability. The island also offers branching paths with different difficulty and rewards, so after each level the player decides whether to take the safer route or risk it for better loot. Each run's level design is procedurally assembled from hand-crafted segments, so the resulting map is different every time while retaining the good pacing and readability typical of metroidvanias. Time-limited gates that only stay open briefly further reward a fast, fluid playthrough.

The game gradually grew through a series of major paid and free expansions, such as Rise of the Giant, Fatal Falls or Return to Castlevania, the latter developed with Konami and bringing a direct crossover with the classic Castlevania series, including its characters and music. Pixel graphics combined with fluid animations create an unusually smooth sense of movement, which also suits portable play very well. Thanks to its addictive progression loop, precise combat and rich post-launch support, Dead Cells became one of the most successful and longest-living indie titles of the generation.

switch__into-breach.article:
**Into the Breach** is a compact turn-based tactics game from the two-person studio Subset Games, creators of the cult hit FTL: Faster Than Light, in which a team of three mechs from the future travels through time to defend the last remnants of humanity against an invasion of giant insects called the Vek. Unlike most tactics games in the XCOM genre, there is no hit-chance randomness here - all actions are entirely deterministic, and the player always sees exactly where and how hard the enemy will strike on their next turn, which makes the game more of a logic puzzle than a game of chance.

The key mechanic is thus prevention rather than direct elimination: it's often better to just push an enemy away from the target it's about to destroy than to kill it, because protected buildings provide the power needed to keep the timeline going. A pushed Vek damages whatever it collides with, so positioning becomes the main weapon, and the player literally builds chains of collisions. Each map is a small, compact grid of a few tiles, but the density of decisions per turn is enormous, and a single mistake can quickly collapse the whole defense. The campaign is short, usually a single longer sitting, and when it falls, one pilot along with their accumulated experience can be sent back in time for a new attempt, elegantly linking failure with the narrative.

The game offers several distinct mech squads with their own abilities and synergies, from ice to fire to electric vehicles, which supports replayability and experimentation with strategies; each squad is essentially a different puzzle ruleset. Minimalist yet imaginative pixel art and a sparse, atmospheric soundtrack complement an overall meditative yet intense experience, which thanks to its short missions suits portable play excellently. Into the Breach is still cited as a textbook example of an elegant, cleanly designed turn-based system without unnecessary complexity, and the Advanced Edition expansion added more mechs, enemies and missions for free.

switch__witcher-3-wild-hunt-complete-edi.article:
Porting the vast open-world RPG **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt** to a handheld console was a technical tour de force in 2019 that many considered impossible, yet the Polish studio Saber Interactive, working with CD Projekt Red, managed to squeeze Geralt of Rivia's entire world into a pocket format through significant but functional reductions in graphical detail. Resolution, draw distance and vegetation density all dropped noticeably, and the frame rate stays at lower values, yet the image remains readable and atmospheric, especially in handheld mode, where the smaller screen elegantly hides some of the compromises. The game follows monster hunter Geralt, who after years is searching for his adopted daughter Ciri, whose extraordinary abilities attract the attention of the supernatural Wild Hunt, while the continent is torn by war between the Nilfgaardian Empire and the northern kingdoms.

The vast world, inspired by Slavic folklore and dark fantasy, offers hundreds of side quests, many of which surpass the main storyline in quality of writing. The elaborate combat system combines swords, magical Signs and alchemy: before a hunt it's worth applying the right oil to your blade, brewing potions and consulting the bestiary, because every monster has a different weakness and a direct confrontation without preparation tends to be short. On top of that come morally ambiguous decisions with no clearly correct answers, whose consequences often only show up many hours later. The Switch version contains all the content, including both major expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, which are often ranked among the very best expansions in the history of the RPG genre.

Due to graphic violence, sexual content and dark themes, the game is clearly intended for an adult audience. Despite the necessary compromises in frame rate and texture detail, the essence of the game - the depth of the story and the free quest structure - remained completely intact, allowing players to experience one of the most acclaimed RPGs in history even on the go. The port became a textbook example proving that for a well-written game, script and design matter more than pixel count.

switch__doom.article:
The 2016 reboot of the legendary **DOOM** series arrived on Switch two years later in a port by Panic Button, a studio specializing in bringing demanding titles to Nintendo hardware, and despite noticeable graphical compromises it retained the brutal pace and gleeful sense of movement that made the original reignite the entire FPS genre. The game returns players to the role of the wordless Doom Slayer, who wakes up on the Martian UAC base flooded with demons from hell after experiments with Argent energy opened a gateway to hellish dimensions on Earth.

Unlike the cover-based, slow-shooting trend popular at the time, DOOM is built on constant aggressive forward movement - the so-called Glory Kills system rewards closing in on a damaged enemy with a brutal, health-restoring finishing animation, forcing the player to keep attacking instead of hiding behind corners. The chainsaw supplements ammo, armor drops from burned enemies, and the result is a closed loop in which retreat is punished and aggression rewarded. An arsenal of weapons from the shotgun through the plasma rifle to the legendary BFG allows each situation to be solved differently, and quickly switching between them on the fly is key to surviving an arena full of demons. The arenas themselves are built vertically, with platforms, jumps and shortcuts that deliberately reference the level design of nineties predecessors. The game also includes multiplayer matches and the SnapMap editor for creating custom maps.

The atmosphere is held together by an industrial metal soundtrack whose guitar riffs kick in exactly when an arena locks down, along with a stylized mix of sci-fi technology and hellish imagery. Due to extreme violence, gore and terrifying imagery, DOOM is clearly aimed at adult players. Bringing such a demanding action game to a handheld console was a technical surprise - resolution and detail did drop, but the fluidity needed for fast action was preserved - cementing Panic Button's reputation as masters of porting.

switch__mario-party-superstars.article:
**Mario Party Superstars** is a nostalgic celebration of the best moments from the series' twenty-year history, assembled from carefully selected boards and minigames from the first five entries released on the Nintendo 64. Instead of experimenting with new rules, the game focuses on returning to the basics fans loved - the classic turn-based journey across boards full of stars and coins, random events, and scheming between players who can steal stars from each other or sabotage progress using items bought from the shopkeeper Kamek.

The five chosen boards, such as Peach's Birthday Cake or Space Land, are among the most beloved in the series' history and have been visually reworked while keeping the original layout and spirit, including the placement of crossroads and traps that longtime fans will recall even after all these years. The collection of one hundred twenty minigames draws from the franchise's entire history and offers variety ranging from quick reflex duels to team challenges to strategic puzzles, with the controls adapted to the modern Joy-Con scheme, eliminating the wild analog-stick spinning that used to wreck Nintendo 64 controllers. Also new is online multiplayer support for both boards and minigames, allowing the game to be played remotely with friends, which previous entries in the series lacked; on top of that come optional rules like a shortened number of turns or turning off the time limit on turns.

Critics praised precisely this return to the proven, less aggressive board design compared to newer entries, which had been accused of excessive randomness. Visually the game relies on clean, colorful graphics and rearranged versions of the original melodies from the Nintendo 64 era, which round off the nostalgic feeling. Mario Party Superstars became a favorite choice for family game nights thanks to its combination of nostalgia, accessibility and a solid amount of content for a reasonable price, and it remains to this day a title that gets pulled out on Switch whenever a bunch of people gather around one TV.

switch__super-mario-rpg.article:
**Super Mario RPG** on Switch is a faithful remake of the legendary 1996 SNES game, then created by Square in collaboration with Nintendo, which laid the foundation for later offshoots like Paper Mario and Mario & Luigi. The story begins when a giant sword named Smithy falls from the sky and shatters the Star Road, interrupting Bowser's wedding to the kidnapped Peach and scattering seven star fragments across the kingdom, which Mario must gather together with new allies like the cloud-like Mallow and the star warrior Geno.

Unlike later platformers, this is a classic turn-based RPG enriched with an action element - by pressing a button at the right moment during an attack or defense, the player increases damage dealt or reduces damage taken, giving battles a rhythmic, almost musical dynamic. The remake made this mechanic clearer with a visual effect on a successful timing and added group attacks charged up through a series of precise hits. World exploration takes place in an isometric view and is interspersed with jumping segments, hidden chests and bizarre side activities from mine-cart rides to rhythm minigames, so the game never falls into a rut of corridors and random battles.

The remake completely redid the graphics into a stylized 3D look while preserving the original level design, dialogue and humor, and added a clearer world map along with minor control improvements. Yoko Shimomura's music, later famous also thanks to the Kingdom Hearts series, ranks among the most iconic in Nintendo's history, and the remake offers it in both a rearranged and the original chiptune version. Thanks to the combination of nostalgia, accessible difficulty and refreshing humor, the remake was warmly received and reminded players just how influential this game was for the entire JRPG genre on Nintendo consoles. Characters like Geno or Mallow have also returned to wider recognition thanks to the remake, even beyond the hardcore fanbase that had been asking for their return for decades.

switch__advance-wars-1-2-re-boot-camp.article:
**Advance Wars 1+2: Re-Boot Camp** is a complete graphical remake of two classic turn-based strategy games, Advance Wars and Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising, originally released on the Game Boy Advance in the early 2000s, a series that had gone without a brand-new entry for nearly a generation. The player commands the armies of warring factions such as Orange Star or Blue Moon across a series of missions set on a clear square grid, managing income from captured cities and factories, building units ranging from infantry through tanks to planes and ships, and exploiting terrain advantages and the rock-paper-scissors-style matchups between unit types.

Each turn is thus a small economic balancing act: money from cities never covers everything, cheap infantry can capture buildings but can't stop tanks on their own, and forests or mountains boost defense enough that a poorly planned attack can cost half an army. A distinctive spice of the series are the CO commanders with unique passive bonuses and powerful, one-time-activatable abilities called CO Powers, which can turn around even a seemingly hopeless battle. The remake completely reworked the visual style into chunky, colorful 3D graphics reminiscent of toys, while keeping exactly the same content, missions, and balance as the original games; fully animated battle sequences and voiced commander lines were added.

The release was not without complications — the game was delayed by a year at the last moment due to the sensitivity of the military-conflict theme at the time of the Russian invasion of Ukraine. The campaign offers dozens of missions across two interconnected campaigns and a full multiplayer mode for battles against friends or AI, complemented by a custom map editor. Re-Boot Camp introduced new generations of players to a genre now represented by only a handful of console titles, and delighted longtime fans with its faithfulness to the original, even though some of them, after years of waiting, would have preferred an entirely new installment.

switch__live-live.article:
**Live A Live** is a remarkable remake of a 1994 Japanese RPG that never officially reached the West and was long considered one of Square's most significant untranslated gems. The game is divided into seven entirely self-contained story chapters set in vastly different historical eras and genres — from a prehistoric tribal adventure through the story of a kung-fu master in a Chinese temple, a Wild West-era western, a sci-fi spaceship tale, to a horror chapter set in modern-day Yokohama burdened by a mysterious crime.

Each chapter has its own protagonist with a distinct play style and pacing: the prehistoric segment gets by almost without written dialogue and relies on smell and pantomime, the western is built around setting traps before a final showdown, and the sci-fi episode approaches a self-contained detective horror where there's no combat for a long stretch. Only after completing all seven stories is a connecting eighth chapter revealed, in which the storylines intersect against a shared enemy across time.
